question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Sosiologi & Sejarah Budaya)

The Weaver of Kembang Goyang

In a quiet neighborhood on the outskirts of Yogyakarta, Ibu Sari was the last artisan still practicing the intricate art of hand-drawn batik tulis using natural indigo dyes. While neighboring workshops had switched to mass-produced printed fabrics to satisfy fast-fashion tourists, Ibu Sari refused to compromise her months-long waxing and dyeing process. However, as bills piled up and young apprentices left for factory jobs in the city, she began to fear that her ancestral craft was doomed to fade into obscurity.

One afternoon, a young architecture student named Dimas visited her workshop while researching sustainable local materials. Fascinated by the geometric precision and botanical chemistry behind Ibu Sari’s patterns, Dimas realized that these motifs were not mere decorations; they were visual records of local philosophy and ecological balance. Yet, he noticed that Ibu Sari struggled to reach buyers who appreciated the cultural depth behind her work.

Instead of asking her to speed up production, Dimas offered to document the storytelling and mathematical symmetry of each cloth through a digital archive and an international exhibition. He paired every finished textile with a detailed narrative explaining the philosophical meaning of its motifs and the months of patience woven into its threads.

When the exhibition opened, collectors and designers were captivated by the authenticity of the pieces, eagerly purchasing the entire collection at fair, sustainable prices. Watching young visitors ask questions about the ancient symbols, Ibu Sari smiled with renewed purpose. She realized that preserving heritage did not require abandoning tradition for speed, but rather translating its timeless meaning for a new generation.

Passage 3: Reusable Launch Vehicles (Saintek)

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Astrofisika & Eksplorasi Antariksa)

For decades, space exploration was constrained by the staggering cost of single-use rockets, which burned up in the atmosphere or crashed into the ocean after a single launch. However, the advent of reusable orbital launch vehicles has fundamentally transformed the economics of spaceflight. By utilizing precision-guided thrusters, aerodynamic grid fins, and autonomous landing software, modern aerospace engineers can now recover and refurbish first-stage boosters within weeks, slashing launch costs by more than half.

This technological breakthrough has catalyzed a booming commercial space sector, enabling universities, startups, and developing nations to deploy small satellites for climate monitoring, global telecommunications, and agricultural mapping. Rather than waiting years for rare government-funded missions, researchers can now access low Earth orbit on a routine basis. Consequently, the democratization of orbital access is accelerating scientific innovation right here on Earth.

Nevertheless, the rapid proliferation of satellite constellations has introduced a pressing environmental challenge in orbit: space debris. With thousands of active and defunct satellites crowding popular orbital pathways, the risk of cascading collisions—known as the Kessler syndrome—threatens to render certain orbital zones unusable for generations. Addressing this hazard requires international regulatory frameworks and active debris-removal technologies to ensure that the new era of spaceflight remains sustainable.

Source: Adapted from European Space Agency (ESA) & NASA Space Technology Reports, "The Economics of Reusable Launch Systems and Orbital Sustainability," 2023.

What is the main idea of the passage?
option_a: Single-use rockets are still more reliable than reusable boosters for launching heavy satellites.
option_b: Reusable rocket technology has lowered spaceflight costs and democratized access to orbit, though it brings new space debris challenges.
option_c: Developing nations are solely responsible for creating dangerous space debris in low Earth orbit.
option_d: The Kessler syndrome has already destroyed all global telecommunications satellites.
option_e: Autonomous landing software is the most expensive component of modern aerospace engineering.
explanation:
Reusable rocket technology has lowered spaceflight costs and democratized access to orbit, though it brings new space debris challenges.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Gagasan utama mencakup dua sisi yang dibahas teks: manfaat revolusioner roket pakai ulang dalam memangkas biaya dan membuka akses orbit (Paragraf 1–2), serta tantangan baru berupa sampah antariksa (Paragraf 3).

(C) Salah: Teks menyebut ribuan satelit secara umum, tidak menyalahkan negara berkembang saja.
(D) Salah: Kessler syndrome adalah ancaman risiko di masa depan, belum menghancurkan seluruh satelit.
(E) Salah: Teks tidak menyatakan bahwa perangkat lunak pendaratan adalah komponen termahal.

Passage 4: Behavioral Economics and "Nudges" (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Ekonomi Perilaku & Kebijakan Publik)

In traditional economic theory, human beings are assumed to be "rational actors" who consistently make decisions that maximize their financial well-being. However, behavioral economists have demonstrated that real-world choices are heavily influenced by cognitive biases, social norms, and the way options are presented—a concept known as "choice architecture." Rather than restricting freedom through strict bans or heavy taxes, governments and organizations increasingly use subtle behavioral interventions called "nudges" to guide people toward beneficial decisions.

A classic example of nudging involves retirement savings and organ donation programs. When employees are automatically enrolled in a pension plan with the option to opt out, participation rates soar compared to systems requiring active sign-up, due to human inertia and the status quo bias. Similarly, placing healthier food options at eye level in school cafeterias significantly increases fruit and vegetable consumption without removing the students' freedom to choose other meals.

While nudges have proven to be cost-effective policy tools, critics raise ethical concerns regarding manipulation and paternalism. Because choice architecture operates subconsciously, poorly regulated nudges could be exploited by corporations to steer consumers into hidden subscriptions or suboptimal financial products—a practice known as "sludging." Therefore, behavioral scientists emphasize that ethical nudging must remain transparent, easily reversible, and genuinely aligned with the individual's long-term welfare.

Source: Adapted from OECD Behavioural Insights Reports & Thaler, R. H., "Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness," 2021.

What is the main idea of the passage?
option_a: Traditional economic theory is completely useless because humans never make logical decisions.
option_b: Behavioral "nudges" subtly guide beneficial decisions without limiting freedom, though they require ethical transparency to prevent manipulation.
option_c: Governments should ban unhealthy foods in school cafeterias instead of using choice architecture.
option_d: Automatic enrollment in pension plans violates employees' basic constitutional rights.
option_e: Corporations use behavioral economics exclusively to help consumers save money for retirement.
explanation:
Behavioral "nudges" subtly guide beneficial decisions without limiting freedom, though they require ethical transparency to prevent manipulation.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Merangkum inti seluruh paragraf: konsep nudge yang mengarahkan pilihan positif tanpa membatasi kebebasan (Paragraf 1–2) serta perlunya transparansi etis agar tidak disalahgunakan menjadi manipulasi/sludging (Paragraf 3).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Teks hanya mengoreksi asumsi ekonomi tradisional, tidak menyebutnya sama sekali tidak berguna.
(C) Salah: Nudging justru menghindari pelarangan ketat ("without removing the students' freedom").
(D) Salah: Tidak ada pembahasan mengenai pelanggaran hak konstitusional.
(E) Salah: Korporasi justru dikritik karena berpotensi mengeksploitasi bias kognitif demi keuntungan sepihak.

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Ekonomi Perilaku & Kebijakan Publik)

In traditional economic theory, human beings are assumed to be "rational actors" who consistently make decisions that maximize their financial well-being. However, behavioral economists have demonstrated that real-world choices are heavily influenced by cognitive biases, social norms, and the way options are presented—a concept known as "choice architecture." Rather than restricting freedom through strict bans or heavy taxes, governments and organizations increasingly use subtle behavioral interventions called "nudges" to guide people toward beneficial decisions.

A classic example of nudging involves retirement savings and organ donation programs. When employees are automatically enrolled in a pension plan with the option to opt out, participation rates soar compared to systems requiring active sign-up, due to human inertia and the status quo bias. Similarly, placing healthier food options at eye level in school cafeterias significantly increases fruit and vegetable consumption without removing the students' freedom to choose other meals.

While nudges have proven to be cost-effective policy tools, critics raise ethical concerns regarding manipulation and paternalism. Because choice architecture operates subconsciously, poorly regulated nudges could be exploited by corporations to steer consumers into hidden subscriptions or suboptimal financial products—a practice known as "sludging." Therefore, behavioral scientists emphasize that ethical nudging must remain transparent, easily reversible, and genuinely aligned with the individual's long-term welfare.

Source: Adapted from OECD Behavioural Insights Reports & Thaler, R. H., "Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness," 2021.

Based on the second paragraph, why does automatic enrollment significantly increase participation in pension plans?
option_a: Because employees are fined heavily if they attempt to opt out of the program.
option_b: Because people tend to stick with default options due to inertia and status quo bias.
option_c: Because pension plans guarantee instant financial returns within the first month.
option_d: Because human resource managers force workers to sign contracts without reading them.
option_e: Because active sign-up systems are illegal in most developed countries.
explanation:
Because people tend to stick with default options due to inertia and status quo bias.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 2 menyebutkan bahwa pendaftaran otomatis meningkatkan partisipasi secara drastis karena adanya inersia manusia (human inertia) dan bias status quo (status quo bias), yaitu kecenderungan bertahan pada pilihan bawaan.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Karyawan tetap bebas keluar (opt out) tanpa denda.
(C) Salah: Tidak ada jaminan imbal hasil instan dalam satu bulan.
(D) Salah: Tidak ada paksaan menandatangani kontrak tanpa membaca.
(E) Salah: Sistem pendaftaran aktif tidak ilegal, hanya tingkat partisipasinya lebih rendah.

question_text:
Passage 1 (Questions 1–5) — Tema: Saintek (Oseanografi & Ekologi Laut)

Deep beneath the ocean's sunlit surface lies the twilight zone, a dimly lit layer stretching from 200 to 1,000 meters down. For decades, marine scientists assumed this cold, high-pressure environment was sparsely populated compared to shallow coral reefs. However, recent acoustic surveys and deep-sea submersibles have revealed a staggering biomass of lanternfish, crustaceans, and gelatinous organisms thriving in these depths. Every night, trillions of these creatures undertake the largest synchronized migration on Earth, swimming upward to feed near the surface before retreating into the darkness at dawn.

This daily vertical migration plays an indispensable role in regulating the global climate. When twilight-zone organisms consume carbon-rich plankton near the surface and return to the depths, they transport vast quantities of carbon away from the atmosphere through their waste and respiration. Scientists estimate that this biological carbon pump sequesters billions of metric tons of carbon dioxide annually, preventing global temperatures from rising far more rapidly than they already are.

Despite its ecological significance, the twilight zone is increasingly targeted by commercial fishing fleets seeking new sources of fishmeal for aquaculture and livestock. Extracting biomass from this fragile ecosystem on an industrial scale could severely disrupt the marine food web that sustains larger predators like tuna and whales. Moreover, depleting these deep-sea populations risks weakening the ocean's natural carbon-trapping mechanism at a critical moment in climate history.

Currently, most of the twilight zone lies in international waters beyond national jurisdictions, leaving it virtually unregulated. Marine conservationists are urging global policymakers to establish precautionary moratoriums on deep-sea trawling until comprehensive ecological assessments are completed. Protecting this hidden frontier is essential not only for preserving deep-sea biodiversity but also for safeguarding Earth's climate stability.

Source: Adapted from Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI), "The Ocean Twilight Zone: Climate and Ecosystem Impacts," 2023.

What is the implied main idea of the first paragraph?
option_a: Shallow coral reefs contain fewer marine species than previously documented by oceanographers.
option_b: The ocean's twilight zone hosts a massive, active ecosystem that defied earlier scientific assumptions.
option_c: Acoustic surveys are the only reliable tools for measuring water pressure in the deep ocean.
option_d: Lanternfish remain permanently in the dark depths to avoid predators near the ocean surface.
option_e: Deep-sea submersibles have disturbed the natural migration patterns of nocturnal sea creatures.
explanation:
The ocean's twilight zone hosts a massive, active ecosystem that defied earlier scientific assumptions.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 1 awalnya menyebutkan asumsi lama ilmuwan bahwa zona senja (twilight zone) sepi kehidupan, lalu membantahnya dengan temuan survei akustik terbaru yang mengungkap biomassa raksasa dan migrasi terbesar di Bumi. Gagasan tersiratnya adalah ekosistem zona ini jauh lebih masif dan aktif dari dugaan sebelumnya.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Terbalik; terumbu karang dangkal dijadikan pembanding awal yang dianggap lebih ramai, bukan lebih sedikit spesiesnya.
(C) Salah: Teks juga menyebut deep-sea submersibles (kapal selam laut dalam), bukan survei akustik saja.
(D) Salah: Lanternfish bermigrasi naik ke permukaan setiap malam untuk makan, tidak diam permanen di kedalaman.
(E) Salah: Kapal selam hanya mengamati/mengungkap migrasi tersebut, bukan mengganggunya.

Passage 2: Endangered Languages (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Linguistik & Antropologi Budaya)

Across the globe, an estimated 7,000 languages are spoken today, yet linguists warn that nearly half of them could vanish by the end of this century. As globalization, urbanization, and digital media increasingly favor a handful of dominant tongues like English, Mandarin, and Spanish, younger generations in minority communities often abandon their ancestral languages. This rapid linguistic shift is frequently driven by economic necessity, as fluency in global languages opens doors to higher education and urban employment.

However, the disappearance of a language represents far more than the loss of vocabulary or grammatical rules. Indigenous languages serve as living repositories of centuries-old ecological knowledge, local history, and unique philosophical worldviews. For instance, many coastal and forest communities possess highly specialized terms for medicinal plants, seasonal weather shifts, and sustainable agriculture that have no direct equivalents in major world languages. When a language dies, humanity loses irreplaceable insights into how to live harmoniously with specific local environments.

To counter this trend, grassroots activists and linguists are leveraging digital technology to revitalize endangered tongues. From developing smartphone keyboard apps for indigenous scripts to recording oral histories on community podcasts, modern tools are helping young speakers reconnect with their linguistic heritage. Additionally, several countries have begun integrating bilingual education into primary schools, recognizing that mother-tongue instruction actually strengthens cognitive development and academic performance.

Sustaining linguistic diversity ultimately requires empowering local communities rather than treating endangered languages as museum artifacts. When indigenous languages are actively used in commerce, governance, and digital entertainment, they regain social prestige and practical relevance. Protecting the world's linguistic mosaic is therefore essential for preserving human cultural resilience in an increasingly homogenized world.

Source: Adapted from UNESCO World Atlas of Languages & National Geographic Society, "Endangered Languages and Cultural Preservation," 2023.

What is the implied main idea of the first paragraph?
option_a: Digital media platforms strictly prohibit users from posting content in minority languages.
option_b: Socioeconomic pressures and globalization are accelerating the widespread extinction of minority languages.
option_c: English, Mandarin, and Spanish are the only languages capable of supporting modern scientific education.
option_d: Urbanization has forced elderly speakers to forget how to communicate in their native tongues.
option_e: Linguists have overestimated the total number of languages currently spoken around the world.
explanation:
Socioeconomic pressures and globalization are accelerating the widespread extinction of minority languages.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 1 menjelaskan ancaman punahnya hampir separuh bahasa dunia akibat globalisasi, urbanisasi, media digital, serta kebutuhan ekonomi generasi muda yang beralih ke bahasa dominan demi pendidikan dan pekerjaan.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Media digital hanya lebih memihak bahasa dominan, bukan melarang penggunaan bahasa minoritas.
(C) Salah: Kata "only" terlalu ekstrem; bahasa global dipilih karena akses ekonomi dan pendidikan tinggi, bukan karena bahasa lain tidak mampu.
(D) Salah: Yang meninggalkan bahasa leluhur adalah generasi muda, bukan penutur lanjut usia yang lupa bahasanya.

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Linguistik & Antropologi Budaya)

Across the globe, an estimated 7,000 languages are spoken today, yet linguists warn that nearly half of them could vanish by the end of this century. As globalization, urbanization, and digital media increasingly favor a handful of dominant tongues like English, Mandarin, and Spanish, younger generations in minority communities often abandon their ancestral languages. This rapid linguistic shift is frequently driven by economic necessity, as fluency in global languages opens doors to higher education and urban employment.

However, the disappearance of a language represents far more than the loss of vocabulary or grammatical rules. Indigenous languages serve as living repositories of centuries-old ecological knowledge, local history, and unique philosophical worldviews. For instance, many coastal and forest communities possess highly specialized terms for medicinal plants, seasonal weather shifts, and sustainable agriculture that have no direct equivalents in major world languages. When a language dies, humanity loses irreplaceable insights into how to live harmoniously with specific local environments.

To counter this trend, grassroots activists and linguists are leveraging digital technology to revitalize endangered tongues. From developing smartphone keyboard apps for indigenous scripts to recording oral histories on community podcasts, modern tools are helping young speakers reconnect with their linguistic heritage. Additionally, several countries have begun integrating bilingual education into primary schools, recognizing that mother-tongue instruction actually strengthens cognitive development and academic performance.

Sustaining linguistic diversity ultimately requires empowering local communities rather than treating endangered languages as museum artifacts. When indigenous languages are actively used in commerce, governance, and digital entertainment, they regain social prestige and practical relevance. Protecting the world's linguistic mosaic is therefore essential for preserving human cultural resilience in an increasingly homogenized world.

Source: Adapted from UNESCO World Atlas of Languages & National Geographic Society, "Endangered Languages and Cultural Preservation," 2023.

Which statement best captures the implied main idea of the second paragraph?
option_a: Major world languages lack the grammatical complexity needed to describe modern agricultural techniques.
option_b: Language extinction erases vital, irreplaceable cultural and environmental wisdom accumulated over generations.
option_c: Medicinal plants can only be discovered by researchers who speak indigenous forest languages.
option_d: Indigenous communities refuse to share their ecological knowledge with outsiders due to historical conflicts.
option_e: Vocabulary loss has minimal impact on a community's understanding of its local history.
explanation:
Language extinction erases vital, irreplaceable cultural and environmental wisdom accumulated over generations.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 2 menekankan bahwa punahnya bahasa bukan sekadar hilangnya kosakata, melainkan hilangnya pengetahuan ekologis kuno (tanaman obat, cuaca, pertanian berkelanjutan) dan sejarah lokal yang tak tergantikan.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Bahasa besar dunia hanya tidak memiliki padanan kata khusus untuk istilah ekologis lokal tertentu, bukan kurang kompleks secara tata bahasa.
(C) Salah: Terlalu mutlak; tanaman obat bisa diteliti secara ilmiah, tetapi pengetahuan tradisional tentangnya tersimpan dalam bahasa asli.
(D) Salah: Tidak ada pembahasan mengenai konflik sejarah yang membuat masyarakat adat menolak berbagi ilmu.
(E) Salah: Bertentangan dengan isi paragraf yang menyatakan bahasa adalah gudang sejarah lokal.

What is the implied main idea of the third paragraph?
option_a: Smartphone applications have completely replaced traditional classroom teachers in remote communities.
option_b: Modern digital tools and bilingual education are being utilized to rescue and promote endangered languages.
option_c: Primary school students struggle academically when taught in both their mother tongue and a global language.
option_d: Recording oral histories on podcasts is more effective than preserving written indigenous scripts.
option_e: Linguists believe that endangered languages can only survive if isolated from modern technology.

Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Aplikasi ponsel hanya membantu generasi muda terhubung kembali dengan bahasanya, bukan menggantikan guru sekolah.
(C) Salah: Pendidikan bahasa ibu justru memperkuat perkembangan kognitif dan prestasi akademik siswa.
(D) Salah: Teks tidak membandingkan mana yang lebih efektif antara podcast dan aksara tulis.
(E) Salah: Justru teknologi modern dimanfaatkan untuk menghidupkan kembali bahasa tersebut.

Passage 3: CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing (Saintek)

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Bioteknologi & Rekayasa Genetika)

For decades, treating genetic disorders such as sickle cell anemia and cystic fibrosis meant managing painful symptoms rather than curing the underlying cause. Today, the emergence of CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing technology has ushered in a revolutionary era in molecular medicine. Derived from a natural defense mechanism found in bacteria, CRISPR acts like a pair of molecular scissors capable of locating and modifying specific sequences of DNA within living cells with unprecedented precision and affordability.

Clinical trials utilizing CRISPR have already yielded remarkable breakthroughs. In recent landmark treatments, physicians extracted bone marrow stem cells from patients with severe blood disorders, edited the faulty gene in a laboratory, and infused the corrected cells back into the patients. Many recipients who previously required frequent blood transfusions have since remained completely symptom-free, demonstrating the transformative potential of targeted genetic therapies.

Despite these medical triumphs, the rapid advancement of gene editing raises complex biological and ethical dilemmas. Scientists warn of "off-target effects," where CRISPR inadvertently alters unintended sections of the genome, potentially triggering harmful mutations or cancer. Furthermore, while editing somatic cells affects only the individual patient, modifying germline cells—such as embryos—creates heritable genetic changes that are passed down to future generations, sparking intense global debate over the prospect of "designer babies."

Navigating the future of genetic medicine demands rigorous safety protocols and international ethical consensus. Regulatory bodies are working to establish clear boundaries that encourage life-saving therapeutic innovations while strictly prohibiting non-medical genetic enhancements. Balancing scientific ambition with moral responsibility will determine how safely humanity wields the power to rewrite its own genetic code.

Source: Adapted from Nature Medicine & Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, "CRISPR Gene Editing: Clinical Breakthroughs and Ethical Frontiers," 2023.

What is the implied main idea of the first paragraph?
option_a: Bacterial infections are the primary cause of hereditary conditions like cystic fibrosis.
option_b: CRISPR-Cas9 technology has transformed genetic medicine by enabling precise, affordable DNA modification.
option_c: Managing chronic symptoms remains more effective than attempting to alter human DNA sequences.
option_d: Molecular scissors can only be used on bacterial cells rather than complex human tissues.
option_e: Traditional pharmaceutical companies invented CRISPR to lower the cost of daily medications.
explanation:
CRISPR-Cas9 technology has transformed genetic medicine by enabling precise, affordable DNA modification.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 1 membandingkan pengobatan lama (hanya meredakan gejala) dengan era baru teknologi CRISPR-Cas9 yang mampu memodifikasi urutan DNA secara presisi dan terjangkau.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Bakteri adalah sumber mekanisme alami CRISPR, bukan penyebab penyakit genetik seperti cystic fibrosis.
(C) Salah: Bertentangan dengan teks yang menyebut CRISPR sebagai era revolusioner dibanding sekadar mengelola gejala.
(D) Salah: CRISPR justru digunakan untuk memodifikasi DNA di dalam sel hidup secara luas, termasuk pada uji klinis manusia.
(E) Salah: CRISPR berasal dari mekanisme pertahanan alami bakteri, bukan diciptakan dari nol oleh perusahaan farmasi untuk obat harian.

Which statement best represents the implied main idea of the second paragraph?
option_a: Bone marrow transplants are no longer necessary for patients suffering from severe blood disorders.
option_b: Early clinical applications of CRISPR have successfully cured previously chronic genetic conditions in patients.
option_c: Laboratory-edited cells lose their effectiveness within a few months of being infused into the bloodstream.
option_d: Blood transfusions remain the safest long-term treatment for individuals with sickle cell anemia.

Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 2 menyajikan bukti keberhasilan uji klinis CRISPR pada pasien kelainan darah parah yang sebelumnya butuh transfusi rutin, kini menjadi bebas gejala sepenuhnya.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Terapi ini justru menggunakan sel punca sumsum tulang (bone marrow stem cells) pasien yang diedit dan dimasukkan kembali.
(C) Salah: Pasien tetap bebas gejala ("remained completely symptom-free"), tidak kehilangan efektivitasnya.
(D) Salah: Transfusi darah adalah metode lama sebelum adanya terapi gen CRISPR.
(E) Salah: Pengeditan gen dilakukan di laboratorium ("edited the faulty gene in a laboratory"), bukan langsung di dalam tubuh.

Passage 4: The 15-Minute City (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Sosiologi Perkotaan & Tata Kota)

Throughout the twentieth century, urban planners across many rapidly growing cities designed infrastructure primarily around the private automobile. Wide multi-lane highways, sprawling suburbs, and vast parking lots became symbols of modern economic progress. However, this car-centric model has increasingly resulted in severe traffic congestion, hazardous air pollution, and fragmented neighborhoods where pedestrians feel unsafe and socially isolated.

In response to these urban challenges, cities from Paris to Seoul are embracing the "15-minute city" concept. Pioneered by urbanist Carlos Moreno, this model reimagines urban neighborhoods so that residents can access all essential daily needs—including workplaces, schools, grocery stores, healthcare, and parks—within a 15-minute walk or bike ride from their homes. By decentralizing urban services and reclaiming road space for bike lanes and pedestrian plazas, cities aim to reduce carbon emissions while revitalizing local community life.

The transition toward walkable, mixed-use neighborhoods also yields substantial economic and public health benefits. Studies show that pedestrian-friendly streets boost foot traffic and revenue for small local businesses compared to car-dominated avenues. At the same time, integrating active transportation into daily routines lowers rates of cardiovascular disease and obesity while fostering spontaneous social interactions among neighbors.

question_text:
Passage 1 (Questions 1–5) — Tema: Saintek (Biomimikri & Rekayasa Material)

For millions of years, living organisms have evolved intricate structural adaptations to survive in harsh environments. Today, engineers and material scientists are increasingly turning to "biomimicry"—the practice of emulating biological designs—to solve complex human engineering challenges. Rather than relying solely on energy-intensive manufacturing or toxic synthetic chemicals, researchers study how nature achieves remarkable strength, flexibility, and efficiency using minimal resources.

A prime example of biomimicry is inspired by the lotus leaf, which remains spotless even in muddy swamps. Under a microscope, the leaf's surface is covered in microscopic wax-coated bumps that repel water droplets, causing them to roll off while picking up dirt particles along the way. By replicating this nanostructure on exterior paints and glass coatings, scientists have developed self-cleaning surfaces that dramatically reduce the need for chemical detergents and manual maintenance.

Another breakthrough stems from studying spider silk, a natural protein fiber that is five times stronger than steel by weight yet remarkably elastic. Attempting to manufacture synthetic equivalents traditionally required extreme heat and hazardous solvents, which often degraded the fiber's strength. However, modern bioengineers have recently learned to mimic the spider's natural spinning process at room temperature using water-based solutions, paving the way for biodegradable medical sutures and lightweight protective gear.

As sustainability becomes a global imperative, biomimicry offers a transformative paradigm shift in industrial design. Instead of viewing nature merely as a warehouse of raw materials to be extracted, modern innovators recognize ecosystems as a living library of proven blueprints. Embracing these time-tested biological strategies allows humanity to build resilient technologies that harmonize with, rather than deplete, the natural world.

Source: Adapted from AskNature (Biomimicry Institute) & MIT News, "Nature-Inspired Engineering and Sustainable Materials," 2023.

Which of the following best restates the sentence "Rather than relying solely on energy-intensive manufacturing or toxic synthetic chemicals, researchers study how nature achieves remarkable strength, flexibility, and efficiency using minimal resources." in the first paragraph?
option_a: Scientists avoid using natural resources because synthetic chemicals are more efficient and flexible for modern manufacturing.
option_b: Instead of depending exclusively on high-energy production and harmful artificial substances, researchers examine how nature creates strong, adaptable, and efficient structures with limited materials.
option_c: Energy-intensive factories are the only way for researchers to replicate the strength and flexibility found in biological organisms.
option_d: Researchers believe that nature wastes too many resources to achieve the strength required by modern synthetic engineering.
option_e: By combining toxic chemicals with minimal natural resources, scientists have eliminated the need for energy-intensive manufacturing.
explanation:
Instead of depending exclusively on high-energy production and harmful artificial substances, researchers examine how nature creates strong, adaptable, and efficient structures with limited materials.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Opsi ini mempertahankan makna dan struktur pertentangan kalimat asli secara akurat melalui padanan kata: "Rather than relying solely" $\rightarrow$ "Instead of depending exclusively", "toxic synthetic chemicals" $\rightarrow$ "harmful artificial substances", dan "using minimal resources" $\rightarrow$ "with limited materials".
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Menyatakan ilmuwan menghindari sumber daya alam karena bahan sintetis lebih efisien (bertolak belakang dengan teks).
(C) Salah: Menyatakan pabrik boros energi adalah satu-satunya cara meniru alam (salah makna).
(D) Salah: Menuduh alam memboroskan sumber daya, padahal teks menyebut alam menggunakan sumber daya minimal.
(E) Salah: Teks menyatakan peneliti tidak bergantung pada bahan kimia beracun, bukan menggabungkannya.

Passage 2: The Circular Economy (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Ekonomi Sirkular & Kebijakan Lingkungan)

For decades, the global economy has operated predominantly on a "linear" model: raw materials are extracted, manufactured into products, used briefly, and ultimately discarded as waste. While this take-make-dispose system fueled rapid industrial growth in the twentieth century, it has resulted in mounting landfills, severe resource depletion, and escalating greenhouse gas emissions. As global consumption continues to rise, economists warn that continuing along this linear trajectory is both ecologically unsustainable and economically risky.

In response, policymakers and business leaders are increasingly advocating for a transition toward a "circular economy." Unlike the linear approach, a circular system is designed to eliminate waste by keeping materials and products in continuous use for as long as possible. Through strategies such as modular product design, repairability, remanufacturing, and closed-loop recycling, items at the end of their service life are recovered and transformed into valuable inputs for new production cycles.

Adopting circular principles offers substantial economic advantages beyond environmental preservation. Companies that transition from selling single-use goods to offering product-as-a-service models—such as leasing heavy machinery or refurbishing electronics—can reduce their vulnerability to volatile raw material prices while fostering long-term customer relationships. Furthermore, expanding repair and recycling infrastructure creates thousands of skilled local jobs that cannot be easily outsourced.

However, achieving a truly circular economy requires overcoming entrenched regulatory and behavioral barriers. Existing tax structures often penalize labor-intensive repair work while subsidizing virgin resource extraction, making new products artificially cheaper than repaired ones. Shifting the global market will therefore demand coordinated policy reforms, corporate accountability, and a cultural shift away from disposable consumerism.

Source: Adapted from Ellen MacArthur Foundation & World Economic Forum, "Completing the Picture: How the Circular Economy Tackles Climate Change," 2022.

Which of the following best restates the sentence "As global consumption continues to rise, economists warn that continuing along this linear trajectory is both ecologically unsustainable and economically risky." in the first paragraph?
option_a: Economists predict that rising global consumption will make the linear economic model safer and more profitable over time.
option_b: With worldwide consumption growing, economists caution that maintaining this linear path threatens environmental stability and poses financial dangers.
option_c: Continuing along a linear trajectory is the only way for economists to prevent ecological collapse caused by rising consumption.
option_d: Economists believe that ecological risks can be ignored as long as global consumption continues to drive industrial growth.
option_e: Rising global consumption has already forced all industries to abandon the economically risky linear model.
explanation:
With worldwide consumption growing, economists caution that maintaining this linear path threatens environmental stability and poses financial dangers.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Mempertahankan hubungan sebab-akibat dan dua risiko utama: "ecologically unsustainable" $\rightarrow$ "threatens environmental stability" dan "economically risky" $\rightarrow$ "poses financial dangers".
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Bertentangan dengan peringatan ekonom bahwa jalur linear justru berisiko secara ekonomi.
(C) Salah: Jalur linear justru memicu kerusakan ekologi, bukan mencegahnya.
(D) Salah: Ekonom memperingatkan bahaya ekologi, bukan mengabaikannya.
(E) Salah: Industri belum sepenuhnya meninggalkan model linear; transisi baru mulai didorong.

Passage 3: Sleep Neuroscience and the Glymphatic System (Saintek)

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Neurosains & Fisiologi Tidur)

Although sleep was once regarded by physiologists as a passive state of neural dormancy, modern neuroimaging has revealed that the sleeping brain is remarkably active. Throughout the night, the brain cycles through distinct stages of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Each stage orchestrates essential restorative processes, ranging from physical tissue repair and hormone regulation to the consolidation of newly acquired memories.

One of the most groundbreaking discoveries in sleep neuroscience involves the "glymphatic system," a macroscopic waste-clearance network in the central nervous system. During deep NREM sleep, brain cells shrink slightly, expanding the interstitial space between neurons by up to 60 percent. This structural expansion allows cerebrospinal fluid to flush out neurotoxic metabolic byproducts—including beta-amyloid proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease—that accumulate during waking hours.

Conversely, chronic sleep deprivation severely impairs both cognitive performance and long-term neurological health. When individuals consistently sleep fewer than seven hours per night, the prefrontal cortex—responsible for executive decision-making and emotional regulation—exhibits diminished activity, while the amygdala becomes hyper-reactive to negative stimuli. Over decades, persistent disruption of the brain's nightly cleansing cycle significantly elevates the risk of neurodegenerative disorders and cardiovascular disease.

Prioritizing consistent, high-quality sleep is therefore not a luxury, but a fundamental biological necessity. Maintaining regular sleep-wake schedules and minimizing exposure to artificial blue light before bedtime help preserve the integrity of natural circadian rhythms. Ultimately, protecting sleep architecture is one of the most effective investments an individual can make for lifelong cognitive vitality.

Source: Adapted from National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) & Nedergaard, M., "The Glymphatic System and Sleep Neurobiology," 2023.

Which of the following best restates the sentence "Although sleep was once regarded by physiologists as a passive state of neural dormancy, modern neuroimaging has revealed that the sleeping brain is remarkably active." in the first paragraph?
option_a: Modern neuroimaging confirms earlier physiological theories that the brain shuts down completely during sleep.
option_b: Even though scientists previously viewed sleep as an inactive period of brain rest, contemporary brain scans show that the brain remains highly dynamic while asleep.
option_c: Physiologists have proven that neural dormancy only occurs when modern neuroimaging equipment is used during REM sleep.
option_d: The sleeping brain is far less active than physiologists originally believed before the invention of neuroimaging.
option_e: Neural dormancy is a modern concept that explains why the brain becomes passive during neuroimaging tests.
explanation:
Even though scientists previously viewed sleep as an inactive period of brain rest, contemporary brain scans show that the brain remains highly dynamic while asleep.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Menjaga kontras (Although $\rightarrow$ Even though) antara pandangan lama (passive state of neural dormancy $\rightarrow$ inactive period of brain rest) dan temuan modern (modern neuroimaging has revealed... remarkably active $\rightarrow$ contemporary brain scans show... remains highly dynamic).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Pencitraan saraf modern justru membantah anggapan bahwa otak mati total saat tidur.
(C) Salah: Neural dormancy adalah anggapan lama yang keliru, bukan fenomena yang terjadi saat pemindaian REM.
(D) Salah: Otak saat tidur jauh lebih aktif dari dugaan semula, bukan lebih pasif.
(E) Salah: Neural dormancy adalah konsep lama fisiolog, bukan konsep modern.

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Neurosains & Fisiologi Tidur)

Although sleep was once regarded by physiologists as a passive state of neural dormancy, modern neuroimaging has revealed that the sleeping brain is remarkably active. Throughout the night, the brain cycles through distinct stages of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Each stage orchestrates essential restorative processes, ranging from physical tissue repair and hormone regulation to the consolidation of newly acquired memories.

One of the most groundbreaking discoveries in sleep neuroscience involves the "glymphatic system," a macroscopic waste-clearance network in the central nervous system. During deep NREM sleep, brain cells shrink slightly, expanding the interstitial space between neurons by up to 60 percent. This structural expansion allows cerebrospinal fluid to flush out neurotoxic metabolic byproducts—including beta-amyloid proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease—that accumulate during waking hours.

Conversely, chronic sleep deprivation severely impairs both cognitive performance and long-term neurological health. When individuals consistently sleep fewer than seven hours per night, the prefrontal cortex—responsible for executive decision-making and emotional regulation—exhibits diminished activity, while the amygdala becomes hyper-reactive to negative stimuli. Over decades, persistent disruption of the brain's nightly cleansing cycle significantly elevates the risk of neurodegenerative disorders and cardiovascular disease.

Prioritizing consistent, high-quality sleep is therefore not a luxury, but a fundamental biological necessity. Maintaining regular sleep-wake schedules and minimizing exposure to artificial blue light before bedtime help preserve the integrity of natural circadian rhythms. Ultimately, protecting sleep architecture is one of the most effective investments an individual can make for lifelong cognitive vitality.

Source: Adapted from National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) & Nedergaard, M., "The Glymphatic System and Sleep Neurobiology," 2023.

option_b: Sticking to consistent sleeping and waking times while reducing pre-bedtime screen light supports the healthy functioning of the body's internal clock.
option_c: Natural circadian rhythms are unaffected by irregular sleep schedules as long as artificial blue light is minimized.
option_d: Artificial blue light is necessary to reset natural circadian rhythms in people with strict sleep-wake schedules.
option_e: Preserving circadian rhythms requires eliminating all natural light exposure and sleeping at random hours.
explanation:
Sticking to consistent sleeping and waking times while reducing pre-bedtime screen light supports the healthy functioning of the body's internal clock.

Passage 4: The Ancient Silk Road (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Sejarah Ekonomi & Globalisasi Awal)

Long before the advent of modern container ships and fiber-optic cables, the ancient Silk Road served as humanity's premier transcontinental network of trade and cultural exchange. Stretching over 6,400 kilometers from East Asia to the Mediterranean basin, this interconnected web of overland caravan trails and maritime routes facilitated the movement of luxury commodities such as Chinese silk, Indian spices, and Roman glassware. Rather than being a single paved highway, the Silk Road operated as a dynamic relay system where merchants traded goods across regional hubs.

Beyond commercial merchandise, the Silk Road functioned as a vital conduit for the diffusion of technologies, philosophies, and scientific knowledge. Paper-making and gunpowder techniques traveled westward from China, fundamentally transforming European literacy and warfare, while mathematical concepts and astronomical instruments moved eastward. Simultaneously, major world religions—including Buddhism, Islam, and Nestorian Christianity—spread along these trade arteries, fostering cosmopolitan cities where diverse languages and traditions coexisted.

However, this unprecedented interconnectedness also carried unforeseen biological and geopolitical consequences. In the fourteenth century, the same trade routes that transported silk and spices inadvertently accelerated the westward spread of the bubonic plague, devastating populations across Asia and Europe. Furthermore, as maritime navigation technologies advanced in the fifteenth century, European powers sought direct sea routes to Asia to bypass overland middlemen, gradually diminishing the economic dominance of traditional Silk Road caravan cities.

Today, historians view the Silk Road as an early blueprint for globalization, demonstrating how commercial interdependence can drive both human innovation and shared vulnerability. Studying its rise and transformation reminds modern societies that global connectivity brings immense cultural enrichment alongside complex systemic risks.

Source: Adapted from UNESCO Silk Roads Programme & Frankopan, P., "The Silk Roads: A New History of the World," 2021.

Which of the following best restates the sentence "Rather than being a single paved highway, the Silk Road operated as a dynamic relay system where merchants traded goods across regional hubs." in the first paragraph?
option_a: The Silk Road consisted of one continuous paved road where individual merchants traveled directly from China to Rome without stopping.
option_b: Instead of a solitary constructed road, the Silk Road functioned as an adaptable network in which traders exchanged merchandise through various regional centers.
option_c: Regional hubs along the Silk Road prevented merchants from trading luxury commodities across different territories.
option_d: Paved highways were built across East Asia to replace the inefficient relay system used by ancient Silk Road merchants.
option_e: Merchants avoided regional hubs because the dynamic relay system made overland trade too dangerous.
explanation:
Instead of a solitary constructed road, the Silk Road functioned as an adaptable network in which traders exchanged merchandise through various regional centers.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: "Rather than being a single paved highway" $\rightarrow$ "Instead of a solitary constructed road", dan "dynamic relay system where merchants traded goods across regional hubs" $\rightarrow$ "adaptable network in which traders exchanged merchandise through various regional centers".
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Bertentangan dengan teks yang menegaskan Jalur Sutra bukan satu jalan raya beraspal tunggal.
(C) Salah: Pusat-pusat regional (regional hubs) justru menjadi tempat pertukaran barang, bukan penghalang.
(D) Salah: Tidak ada pembangunan jalan raya beraspal untuk menggantikan sistem estafet.
(E) Salah: Pedagang justru memanfaatkan pusat regional tersebut untuk berdagang.

question_text:
Passage 1 (Questions 1–5) — Tema: Saintek (Energi Terbarukan & Geologi)

Beneath the Earth's crust lies an immense reservoir of thermal energy generated by the radioactive decay of minerals and residual heat from the planet's formation. Unlike solar and wind power, which fluctuate depending on weather conditions and time of day, geothermal energy provides a continuous, reliable supply of baseload electricity. By drilling deep wells into underground reservoirs of hot water and steam, geothermal power plants can drive turbines twenty-four hours a day with minimal carbon emissions.

Historically, commercial geothermal energy was restricted to volcanically active regions along tectonic plate boundaries, such as Iceland, Indonesia, and parts of the western United States. In these areas, natural underground heat sits close to the surface, making extraction economically viable. However, regions without natural hydrothermal reservoirs were largely unable to tap into this clean energy source due to the prohibitive cost and technical difficulty of drilling through miles of solid granite.

Recent breakthroughs in Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) are rapidly expanding the geographical potential of geothermal power. Borrowed from drilling techniques developed in the oil and gas industry, EGS involves injecting high-pressure fluid deep into hot, impermeable rock formations to create artificial fractures. Water is then circulated through these engineered cracks, absorbing heat before returning to the surface to generate electricity.

If EGS technologies continue to scale and decline in cost, geothermal power could transition from a niche regional resource into a cornerstone of global decarbonization. Because geothermal facilities require significantly smaller land footprints than massive solar farms or wind turbine arrays, they offer an efficient pathway for nations seeking to achieve net-zero emissions without sacrificing vast tracts of agricultural or natural land.

Source: Adapted from U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) & International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), "The Future of Enhanced Geothermal Systems," 2023.

What can be concluded from the first paragraph regarding geothermal energy compared to solar and wind power?
option_a: Geothermal energy produces higher carbon emissions than wind turbines during cloudy weather.
option_b: Geothermal energy offers greater consistency in power generation because it does not depend on atmospheric conditions.
option_c: Solar and wind power are completely incapable of generating electricity during daytime hours.
option_d: Geothermal power plants can only operate for a few hours each day to prevent mineral decay.
option_e: Radioactive decay inside the Earth's crust makes geothermal electricity too dangerous for residential use.
explanation:
Geothermal energy offers greater consistency in power generation because it does not depend on atmospheric conditions.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 1 mengontraskan tenaga surya dan angin yang berfluktuasi mengikuti cuaca/waktu dengan energi panas bumi yang mampu memasok listrik beban dasar (baseload electricity) terus-menerus selama 24 jam tanpa terpengaruh kondisi atmosfer.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Pembangkit panas bumi menghasilkan emisi karbon minimal (minimal carbon emissions), bukan lebih tinggi dari turbin angin.
(C) Salah: Tenaga surya justru bekerja optimal di siang hari; teks hanya menyebut outputnya berfluktuasi.
(D) Salah: Pembangkit panas bumi beroperasi 24 jam sehari, bukan beberapa jam saja.
(E) Salah: Peluruhan radioaktif alami di bawah kerak Bumi adalah sumber panasnya, bukan bahaya bagi rumah tangga.

Passage 2: The Silent Crowd on Merdeka Avenue (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Psikologi Sosial & Perilaku Kolektif)

The Silent Crowd on Merdeka Avenue

During rush hour on Merdeka Avenue, a crowded commercial street, an elderly street musician named Pak Budi suddenly collapsed onto the pavement, clutching his chest. Dozens of commuters, shopkeepers, and students paused momentarily, glancing at the motionless man before nervously looking around at one another. Because no one else stepped forward immediately, most pedestrians assumed the situation was not a genuine medical emergency or that someone more qualified would intervene. Minutes ticked by as people hurried past, each believing their individual action was unnecessary in such a dense crowd.

Inside a nearby bookstore, a university student named Rina noticed the gathering crowd through the glass window. Initially, she hesitated, experiencing the same social pressure to remain passive like everyone else on the sidewalk. However, recalling a social psychology lecture on the "bystander effect"—the phenomenon where individuals are less likely to help a victim when other people are present—Rina realized that responsibility was being diffused among the onlookers.

Breaking free from the crowd's collective paralysis, Rina rushed outside and knelt beside Pak Budi. Instead of shouting a vague plea for help into the air, she pointed directly at a man in a security uniform and instructed him to call an ambulance, while asking a shopkeeper nearby to bring water. Once Rina took decisive action and assigned clear roles, several bystanders immediately stepped forward to assist, shielding Pak Budi from the sun until paramedics arrived.

Later at the hospital, the attending doctor informed Rina that her prompt intervention had prevented a fatal cardiac arrest. Walking home that evening, Rina reflected on how easily social conformity can blind good people to urgent human need, and how a single person's willingness to take responsibility can shatter the illusion of shared inaction.

Source: Adapted from American Psychological Association (APA) & Darley, J. M., & Latané, B., "Bystander Intervention in Emergencies: Diffusion of Responsibility," 2022.

Based on the first paragraph, what can be concluded about why pedestrians initially failed to help Pak Budi?
option_a: They were angry at Pak Budi for blocking the sidewalk during busy rush hour traffic.
option_b: The presence of many onlookers created a false assumption that the situation was not urgent or that others would act.
option_c: Commuters on Merdeka Avenue are legally prohibited from touching injured strangers before paramedics arrive.
option_d: Nobody on the street noticed Pak Budi collapse because everyone was staring at their smartphones.
option_e: Shopkeepers advised pedestrians to ignore the man until he regained consciousness on his own.
explanation:
The presence of many onlookers created a false assumption that the situation was not urgent or that others would act.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 1 menjelaskan bahwa karena kerumunan orang hanya saling melirik dan tidak ada yang bertindak duluan, para pejalan kaki berasumsi situasi itu bukan darurat medis yang nyata atau orang lain yang lebih kompeten akan menolong.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Tidak ada rasa marah dari pejalan kaki karena trotoar terhalang.
(C) Salah: Tidak ada larangan hukum bagi warga untuk menolong orang pingsan.
(D) Salah: Pejalan kaki melihat Pak Budi jatuh (glancing at the motionless man), bukan sibuk menatap ponsel.
(E) Salah: Pemilik toko juga hanya terdiam ragu, tidak menyuruh orang mengabaikan korban.

Passage 3: Exoplanets and Biosignatures (Saintek)

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Astronomi & Astrobiologi)

For centuries, humanity wondered whether planets existed beyond our solar system. Since the first confirmed discovery of an exoplanet orbiting a Sun-like star in 1995, space telescopes such as Kepler and James Webb have identified more than 5,500 worlds scattered across our galaxy. These distant planets range from scorching gas giants orbiting perilously close to their host stars to rocky, Earth-sized worlds residing within the "habitable zone"—the orbital region where temperatures allow liquid water to exist on a planetary surface.

Detecting these distant worlds is extraordinarily challenging because planets do not emit their own light and are overwhelmingly outshined by their host stars. Astronomers primarily rely on indirect methods, such as the "transit method," which measures the minuscule dip in a star's brightness when an orbiting planet passes directly in front of it. By analyzing the starlight that filters through an exoplanet's atmosphere during a transit, scientists can identify the chemical fingerprints of gases like water vapor, carbon dioxide, and methane.

The ultimate goal of modern exoplanet research is to detect "biosignatures"—atmospheric gas combinations that strongly indicate the presence of living organisms. On Earth, the simultaneous abundance of oxygen and methane is maintained largely by biological activity, as these two gases would otherwise react and destroy each other over time. Finding a similar chemical disequilibrium on a rocky exoplanet would provide compelling evidence that life exists elsewhere in the universe.

However, astrobiologists caution that interpreting atmospheric data requires extreme rigor to avoid false positives. Geological processes, such as volcanic outgassing or ultraviolet radiation splitting water molecules, can occasionally mimic biological gas signatures on lifeless worlds. Therefore, confirming extraterrestrial life will require cross-verifying multiple atmospheric indicators alongside a planet's geological context.

Source: Adapted from NASA Exoplanet Exploration Program & Nature Astronomy, "Atmospheric Biosignatures and the Search for Habitable Worlds," 2023.

Based on the first paragraph, what can be concluded about exoplanets located in the "habitable zone"?
option_a: They are exclusively massive gas giants that orbit extremely close to their host stars.
option_b: Their distance from their host stars creates thermal conditions potentially suitable for surface liquid water.
option_c: All 5,500 exoplanets discovered so far are located inside this habitable orbital region.
option_d: They were all discovered before 1995 using ground-based optical telescopes.
option_e: They emit bright light of their own, making them easy to photograph directly from Earth.
explanation:
Their distance from their host stars creates thermal conditions potentially suitable for surface liquid water.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 1 mendefinisikan habitable zone sebagai wilayah orbit di mana suhu memungkinkan air cair (liquid water) bertahan di permukaan planet.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Planet di zona layak huni dijelaskan sebagai planet berbatu seukuran Bumi (rocky, Earth-sized worlds), bukan raksasa gas panas.
(C) Salah: Angka 5.500 adalah total seluruh eksoplanet yang ditemukan (termasuk raksasa gas panas), bukan semuanya di zona layak huni.
(D) Salah: Eksoplanet pertama baru dikonfirmasi pada tahun 1995 menggunakan teleskop luar angkasa seperti Kepler dan James Webb.
(E) Salah: Paragraf 2 justru menyatakan planet tidak memancarkan cahaya sendiri (do not emit their own light).

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Astronomi & Astrobiologi)

For centuries, humanity wondered whether planets existed beyond our solar system. Since the first confirmed discovery of an exoplanet orbiting a Sun-like star in 1995, space telescopes such as Kepler and James Webb have identified more than 5,500 worlds scattered across our galaxy. These distant planets range from scorching gas giants orbiting perilously close to their host stars to rocky, Earth-sized worlds residing within the "habitable zone"—the orbital region where temperatures allow liquid water to exist on a planetary surface.

Detecting these distant worlds is extraordinarily challenging because planets do not emit their own light and are overwhelmingly outshined by their host stars. Astronomers primarily rely on indirect methods, such as the "transit method," which measures the minuscule dip in a star's brightness when an orbiting planet passes directly in front of it. By analyzing the starlight that filters through an exoplanet's atmosphere during a transit, scientists can identify the chemical fingerprints of gases like water vapor, carbon dioxide, and methane.

The ultimate goal of modern exoplanet research is to detect "biosignatures"—atmospheric gas combinations that strongly indicate the presence of living organisms. On Earth, the simultaneous abundance of oxygen and methane is maintained largely by biological activity, as these two gases would otherwise react and destroy each other over time. Finding a similar chemical disequilibrium on a rocky exoplanet would provide compelling evidence that life exists elsewhere in the universe.

However, astrobiologists caution that interpreting atmospheric data requires extreme rigor to avoid false positives. Geological processes, such as volcanic outgassing or ultraviolet radiation splitting water molecules, can occasionally mimic biological gas signatures on lifeless worlds. Therefore, confirming extraterrestrial life will require cross-verifying multiple atmospheric indicators alongside a planet's geological context.

Source: Adapted from NASA Exoplanet Exploration Program & Nature Astronomy, "Atmospheric Biosignatures and the Search for Habitable Worlds," 2023.

option_a: Because oxygen and methane freeze into solid ice when exposed to starlight.
option_b: Because these gases naturally destroy each other, so their coexistence suggests continuous replenishment by living organisms.
option_c: Because lifeless planets produce vast amounts of oxygen and methane through daily meteor impacts.
option_d: Because the combination of oxygen and methane proves that intelligent civilizations are burning fossil fuels.
option_e: Because Earth is the only planet in the universe where oxygen and methane react chemically.
explanation:
Because these gases naturally destroy each other, so their coexistence suggests continuous replenishment by living organisms.

(A) Salah: Teks tidak menyebut kedua gas tersebut membeku menjadi es akibat cahaya bintang.
(C) Salah: Dunia tak bernyawa tidak menghasilkan kombinasi melimpah keduanya lewat tumbukan meteor harian.
(D) Salah: Biosignature merujuk pada organisme hidup secara umum (seperti mikroba/tumbuhan), bukan peradaban cerdas pembakar bahan bakar fosil.
(E) Salah: Reaksi kimia antara oksigen dan metana adalah hukum kimia universal, bukan hanya terjadi di Bumi.

Passage 4: The Stone Ledger of Desa Tenganan (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Antropologi Budaya & Sejarah Lokal)

The Stone Ledger of Desa Tenganan

In the highland village of Desa Tenganan, an ancient customary council governed water distribution and forest harvesting through a strict code engraved on weathered stone tablets. For generations, every family received an equal share of spring water for their terraced rice fields, provided they participated in maintaining the stone irrigation channels. Young Pak Wayan, who had recently returned from studying agribusiness in the city, viewed this communal arrangement as outdated and inefficient.

Eager to maximize agricultural profits, Wayan proposed privatizing the upper water channels and introducing a metered payment system so wealthier farmers could purchase extra water for cash crops. During the monthly village assembly, he presented spreadsheets projecting a thirty percent increase in total harvest revenue. Impressed by the numbers, several younger landowners supported his plan, arguing that modern market efficiency should replace ancestral rules.

However, the village elders objected, reminding the assembly of the "Great Drought of 1942" recorded on the stone ledger. During that multi-year dry spell, villages that treated water as a private commodity experienced bitter conflicts, hoarding, and total crop failure for poorer families, whereas Tenganan survived because its strict rationing ensured every field received just enough moisture to endure. The elders warned that monetizing water would fracture community solidarity and leave the village defenseless during future climate extremes.

Listening to the historical testimony, Wayan realized his economic model had accounted only for ideal weather conditions while ignoring long-term ecological and social resilience. He withdrew his privatization proposal and instead suggested using his agribusiness training to help the village market its organic heritage rice at premium prices while keeping the communal water system intact.

Source: Adapted from Bali Cultural Heritage & Subak Irrigation Studies (UNESCO World Heritage Centre), "Customary Water Governance and Community Resilience," 2022.

Based on the first paragraph, what can be concluded about Desa Tenganan's traditional water system?
option_a: Wealthy landowners were allowed to take unlimited water without maintaining the channels.
option_b: Access to irrigation water was distributed equally in exchange for shared community labor.
option_c: The stone tablets prohibited villagers from growing rice on terraced hillsides.
option_d: Pak Wayan invented the communal irrigation system after graduating from university.
option_e: Spring water was sold to neighboring villages to fund the customary council.
explanation:
Access to irrigation water was distributed equally in exchange for shared community labor.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 1 menyebutkan bahwa setiap keluarga menerima bagian mata air yang sama untuk sawah terasering mereka, dengan syarat ikut merawat saluran irigasi batu bersama-sama (provided they participated in maintaining...).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Sistem adat memberikan bagian yang sama (equal share) dan mewajibkan partisipasi pemeliharaan bagi semua keluarga.
(C) Salah: Prasasti batu mengatur pembagian air untuk sawah terasering, bukan melarang menanam padi.
(D) Salah: Sistem irigasi komunal tersebut sudah berjalan turun-temurun (For generations), bukan diciptakan Pak Wayan.
(E) Salah: Air digunakan untuk sawah warga desa sendiri, tidak dijual ke desa tetangga.

question_text:
Passage 1 (Questions 1–5) — Tema: Saintek (Komputasi Kuantum & Keamanan Siber)

Classical computers, which power everything from smartphones to supercomputers, process information using binary bits that exist strictly as either a zero or a one. In contrast, quantum computers harness the principles of quantum mechanics to operate with "qubits," which can exist in multiple states simultaneously through a phenomenon known as superposition. This unique capability allows quantum processors to perform complex calculations exponentially faster than even the most advanced classical machines.

While quantum computing promises revolutionary breakthroughs in drug discovery, climate modeling, and financial optimization, it also poses an unprecedented threat to modern cybersecurity. Most current digital encryption methods rely on mathematical problems—such as factoring massive prime numbers—that would take classical computers thousands of years to crack. However, a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could solve these cryptographic puzzles in mere hours, potentially exposing sensitive banking records, medical files, and government communications.

To counter this impending vulnerability, cryptographers worldwide are racing to develop "post-quantum cryptography" (PQC). Unlike quantum key distribution, which requires specialized optical hardware, PQC consists of upgraded mathematical algorithms designed to run on existing classical infrastructure while remaining resistant to quantum attacks. Standardization agencies have already begun urging corporations and public institutions to inventory their encrypted data and initiate the transition toward quantum-resistant protocols.

Migrating global digital infrastructure to post-quantum security will undoubtedly be a complex, multi-year endeavor. Nevertheless, cybersecurity experts warn that delaying this transition could allow malicious actors to harvest encrypted data today with the intention of decrypting it once functional quantum computers become commercially available.

Passage 2: Behavioral Economics and Nudging (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Ekonomi Perilaku & Kebijakan Publik)

The Cafeteria Experiment at Nusantara High

At Nusantara High School, administrator Ibu Sari noticed a troubling trend in the student cafeteria: despite offering fresh fruit cups and whole-grain wraps alongside sugary pastries and fried snacks, nearly eighty percent of students consistently chose the less nutritious options. Simply displaying nutritional posters on the walls had failed to alter student eating habits, prompting Ibu Sari to consult Pak Dimas, a behavioral economist from a nearby university.

Rather than banning junk food or imposing higher prices on sugary treats, Pak Dimas proposed redesigning the cafeteria's "choice architecture"—a concept from behavioral economics known as nudging. He explained that human decision-making is heavily influenced by convenience, visual placement, and default options rather than purely rational calculation. Under his guidance, cafeteria staff placed fresh fruit bowls at eye level near the cash registers, moved pastries to opaque containers at the back counter, and made bottled water the default beverage in lunch combos.

Within six weeks of implementing these subtle environmental adjustments, fruit consumption among students rose by forty-five percent, while pastry sales dropped significantly. Crucially, students never felt their freedom of choice was restricted, because unhealthy snacks remained available for anyone willing to walk to the back counter to request them.

Reflecting on the project's success, Ibu Sari realized that effective public policy does not always require strict mandates or punitive taxes. By thoughtfully structuring everyday environments so that beneficial choices become the easiest ones, institutions can gently guide individuals toward healthier, more sustainable behaviors.

Source: Adapted from Thaler, R. H., & Sunstein, C. R., "Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness" & Behavioural Insights Team (BIT), 2022.

Which of the following best restates the sentence "Simply displaying nutritional posters on the walls had failed to alter student eating habits, prompting Ibu Sari to consult Pak Dimas, a behavioral economist from a nearby university." in the first paragraph?
option_a: Putting up healthy food signs did not change what students ate, which led Ibu Sari to seek advice from Pak Dimas, a local university behavioral economist.
option_b: Nutritional posters successfully improved student diets, so Ibu Sari invited Pak Dimas to celebrate the cafeteria's achievement.
option_c: Pak Dimas advised Ibu Sari to hang more nutritional posters on the cafeteria walls to discourage students from eating fried snacks.
option_d: Students ignored the nutritional posters because Pak Dimas prohibited them from reading signs in the cafeteria.
option_e: Ibu Sari consulted a behavioral economist after nutritional posters caused students to stop buying whole-grain wraps.
explanation:
Putting up healthy food signs did not change what students ate, which led Ibu Sari to seek advice from Pak Dimas, a local university behavioral economist.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Menjaga urutan sebab-akibat: "Simply displaying nutritional posters... failed to alter student eating habits" $\rightarrow$ "Putting up healthy food signs did not change what students ate", dan "prompting Ibu Sari to consult Pak Dimas" $\rightarrow$ "which led Ibu Sari to seek advice from Pak Dimas".
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(B) Salah: Poster nutrisi gagal mengubah kebiasaan makan siswa, bukan berhasil.
(C) Salah: Pak Dimas mengusulkan perubahan tata letak pilihan (choice architecture), bukan menambah poster.
(D) Salah: Tidak ada larangan membaca poster dari Pak Dimas.
(E) Salah: Poster nutrisi tidak menyebabkan siswa berhenti membeli whole-grain wraps.

Passage 3: The Human Gut Microbiome (Saintek)

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Mikrobiologi & Imunologi Manusia)

For much of medical history, bacteria residing inside the human body were viewed primarily as harmful pathogens that needed to be eradicated. However, over the past two decades, advances in DNA sequencing have revealed that the human gastrointestinal tract hosts trillions of beneficial microorganisms—collectively known as the gut microbiome—that play a vital role in maintaining overall health. Far from being passive passengers, these microbial communities synthesize essential vitamins, break down complex dietary fibers, and train the immune system to distinguish between harmless substances and dangerous invaders.

A balanced, diverse gut microbiome acts as a biological shield against chronic inflammation and metabolic disorders. When beneficial gut bacteria ferment soluble fiber from plant-based foods, they produce short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) such as butyrate, which nourish the cells lining the intestinal wall and strengthen the gut barrier. Conversely, diets dominated by ultra-processed foods, refined sugars, and low fiber starve these beneficial microbes, leading to a condition called "dysbiosis"—an imbalance linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes, and autoimmune conditions.

Furthermore, emerging neurobiological research has uncovered a bidirectional communication highway connecting the digestive tract and the central nervous system, known as the "gut-brain axis." Gut microbes produce neurotransmitters—including nearly ninety percent of the body's serotonin—that influence mood, stress resilience, and cognitive clarity. Disruptions to microbial diversity can therefore manifest not only as digestive discomfort, but also as heightened anxiety and depressive symptoms.

Protecting this internal ecosystem requires deliberate lifestyle choices, particularly regarding diet and medication use. While antibiotics remain indispensable for treating severe bacterial infections, their indiscriminate overuse wipes out beneficial gut flora alongside harmful pathogens, underscoring the need for targeted medical prescriptions and fiber-rich nutrition.

Source: Adapted from Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health & Nature Reviews Microbiology, "The Human Gut Microbiome in Health and Disease," 2023.

Which of the following best restates the sentence "Far from being passive passengers, these microbial communities synthesize essential vitamins, break down complex dietary fibers, and train the immune system to distinguish between harmless substances and dangerous invaders." in the first paragraph?
option_a: Rather than merely existing idly in the body, gut microbes actively produce vital nutrients, digest tough plant fibers, and teach immune defenses to tell safe materials apart from threats.
option_b: Microbial communities remain completely inactive inside the digestive tract until dangerous invaders destroy the immune system.
option_c: Because gut bacteria are passive passengers, the human immune system must synthesize essential vitamins on its own.
option_d: Complex dietary fibers prevent microbial communities from distinguishing between harmless substances and dangerous pathogens.
option_e: Training the immune system requires eliminating all microbial communities that break down dietary fibers.
explanation:
Rather than merely existing idly in the body, gut microbes actively produce vital nutrients, digest tough plant fibers, and teach immune defenses to tell safe materials apart from threats.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: "Far from being passive passengers" $\rightarrow$ "Rather than merely existing idly in the body", "synthesize essential vitamins" $\rightarrow$ "produce vital nutrients", dan "distinguish between harmless substances and dangerous invaders" $\rightarrow$ "tell safe materials apart from threats".
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(B) Salah: Mikroba usus bekerja aktif setiap saat, bukan pasif menunggu serangan patogen.
(C) Salah: Mikroba usus bukanlah penumpang pasif, dan merekalah yang membantu mensintesis vitamin penting.
(D) Salah: Serat pangan justru difermentasi oleh mikroba untuk kesehatan usus, bukan menghalangi kerja sistem imun.
(E) Salah: Mikroba usus justru melatih sistem imun; menghilangkannya akan merusak kekebalan tubuh.

option_a: Eating ultra-processed foods and refined sugars nourishes helpful gut bacteria and prevents metabolic illnesses like type 2 diabetes.
