Passage 4: Digital Conservation of Cave Art (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Arkeologi & Konservasi Budaya Digital)

Preserving the Fading Murals of Goa Leang-Leang

Deep inside the limestone karst caves of Maros-Pangkep in South Sulawesi, prehistoric hand stencils and dynamic hunting scenes painted over forty-five thousand years ago adorn the cavern walls. For millennia, these ancient rock art panels survived undisturbed in the stable microclimate of the caves. Recently, however, archaeologist Dr. Hendra and his conservation team documented an alarming acceleration in surface exfoliation, where mineral crusts blister and flake away due to rising temperatures and extreme seasonal humidity linked to climate change.

Realizing that physical restoration alone could not halt the geological weathering of the limestone walls, Dr. Hendra initiated an urgent digital preservation project. Using high-resolution laser scanning and photogrammetry, his team captured sub-millimeter three-dimensional models of every cave chamber and pigment layer. These digital twins record not only the exact geometry and color spectrum of the artwork, but also microscopic tool marks left by Paleolithic artists.

Beyond safeguarding the murals against physical loss, the three-dimensional archive has democratized access to cultural heritage. Previously, strict conservation rules limited cave entry to a handful of researchers to prevent human breath and body heat from accelerating wall decay. Now, students, scholars, and global museum visitors can explore interactive virtual reconstructions of the caves without placing fragile prehistoric surfaces at risk.

Reflecting on the mission, Dr. Hendra emphasized that digital conservation is not a substitute for protecting physical heritage sites, but rather an essential insurance policy. By pairing climate adaptation strategies on the ground with meticulous digital documentation, humanity can ensure that its earliest artistic expressions endure for future generations.

Source: Adapted from Aubert, M. et al., Nature ("Pleistocene Cave Art in Sulawesi") & UNESCO World Heritage Centre Digital Conservation Reports, 2023.

Which of the following best restates the sentence "Recently, however, archaeologist Dr. Hendra and his conservation team documented an alarming acceleration in surface exfoliation, where mineral crusts blister and flake away due to rising temperatures and extreme seasonal humidity linked to climate change." in the first paragraph?
option_a: Lately, Dr. Hendra's team recorded a worrying speedup in rock surface peeling, caused by climate-driven heat and severe seasonal moisture changes.
option_b: Dr. Hendra discovered that rising temperatures and seasonal humidity help stabilize mineral crusts on ancient cave walls.
option_c: Surface exfoliation has slowed down recently because climate change eliminated extreme humidity inside the limestone caves.
option_d: Archaeologists recently painted new hunting scenes over the blistering mineral crusts to protect the cave walls from heat.
option_e: For millennia, extreme seasonal humidity prevented prehistoric hand stencils from surviving inside the Maros-Pangkep caves.
explanation:
Lately, Dr. Hendra's team recorded a worrying speedup in rock surface peeling, caused by climate-driven heat and severe seasonal moisture changes.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: "alarming acceleration in surface exfoliation, where mineral crusts blister and flake away" diparafrasekan menjadi "worrying speedup in rock surface peeling", dan "rising temperatures and extreme seasonal humidity linked to climate change" menjadi "climate-driven heat and severe seasonal moisture changes".
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(B) Salah: Kenaikan suhu dan kelembapan ekstrem justru merusak dan mengelupaskan kerak mineral, bukan menstabilkannya.
(C) Salah: Pengelupasan permukaan justru semakin cepat (acceleration), bukan melambat.
(D) Salah: Tim arkeolog mendokumentasikan kerusakan, bukan melukis adegan berburu baru di atas dinding gua.
(E) Salah: Lukisan prasejarah bertahan selama ribuan tahun berkat iklim mikro gua yang stabil sebelum perubahan iklim terjadi.

For millennia, these ancient rock art panels survived undisturbed in the stable microclimate of the caves. Recently, however, archaeologist Dr. Hendra and his conservation team documented an alarming acceleration in surface exfoliation, where mineral crusts blister and flake away due to rising temperatures and extreme seasonal humidity linked to climate change.

Realizing that physical restoration alone could not halt the geological weathering of the limestone walls, Dr. Hendra initiated an urgent digital preservation project. Using high-resolution laser scanning and photogrammetry, his team captured sub-millimeter three-dimensional models of every cave chamber and pigment layer. These digital twins record not only the exact geometry and color spectrum of the artwork, but also microscopic tool marks left by Paleolithic artists.

Beyond safeguarding the murals against physical loss, the three-dimensional archive has democratized access to cultural heritage. Previously, strict conservation rules limited cave entry to a handful of researchers to prevent human breath and body heat from accelerating wall decay. Now, students, scholars, and global museum visitors can explore interactive virtual reconstructions of the caves without placing fragile prehistoric surfaces at risk.

Reflecting on the mission, Dr. Hendra emphasized that digital conservation is not a substitute for protecting physical heritage sites, but rather an essential insurance policy. By pairing climate adaptation strategies on the ground with meticulous digital documentation, humanity can ensure that its earliest artistic expressions endure for future generations.

Source: Adapted from Aubert, M. et al., Nature ("Pleistocene Cave Art in Sulawesi") & UNESCO World Heritage Centre Digital Conservation Reports, 2023.

Which of the following best restates the sentence "Now, students, scholars, and global museum visitors can explore interactive virtual reconstructions of the caves without placing fragile prehistoric surfaces at risk." in the third paragraph?
option_a: Today, learners, academics, and international museum guests can experience digital 3D versions of the caverns safely without endangering delicate ancient walls.
option_b: Interactive virtual reconstructions have replaced physical museums, forcing students and scholars to visit the fragile caves in person.
option_c: Fragile prehistoric surfaces are now placed at greater risk whenever global museum visitors explore virtual cave reconstructions.
option_d: Only specialized scholars are permitted to view the interactive virtual reconstructions due to the fragility of the prehistoric surfaces.
option_e: Students and visitors must sign waivers accepting the risk of damaging prehistoric walls before using virtual reconstructions.
explanation:
Today, learners, academics, and international museum guests can experience digital 3D versions of the caverns safely without endangering delicate ancient walls.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: "students, scholars, and global museum visitors" $\rightarrow$ "learners, academics, and international museum guests", "interactive virtual reconstructions" $\rightarrow$ "digital 3D versions", dan "without placing fragile prehistoric surfaces at risk" $\rightarrow$ "safely without endangering delicate ancient walls".
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(B) Salah: Rekonstruksi virtual memungkinkan kunjungan jarak jauh tanpa harus masuk ke gua fisik yang rapuh.
(C) Salah: Kunjungan virtual justru menghilangkan risiko kerusakan pada dinding gua asli.
(D) Salah: Akses virtual kini terbuka luas bagi pelajar, akademisi, dan pengunjung museum global, bukan peneliti khusus saja.
(E) Salah: Tidak ada penandatanganan surat pernyataan risiko karena pengunjung mengaksesnya secara virtual.

question_text:
Passage 1 (Questions 1–5) — Tema: Saintek (Bioteknologi & Rekayasa Genetika)

Text 1 The discovery of CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing technology has revolutionized molecular biology by allowing scientists to modify specific DNA sequences with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Acting like molecular scissors, the Cas9 enzyme guided by a synthetic RNA molecule can cut targeted sections of a genome to disable harmful mutations or insert beneficial genes. In agriculture, researchers have already used this tool to develop drought-resistant wheat and disease-immune livestock, offering vital solutions for global food security.

In medicine, clinical trials utilizing CRISPR have achieved remarkable milestones in treating inherited blood disorders such as sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. By extracting a patient's bone marrow stem cells, editing the faulty gene in a laboratory, and infusing the corrected cells back into the body, doctors have successfully eliminated painful symptoms in numerous patients. Many geneticists believe this precision therapy could eventually cure thousands of previously untreatable monogenic diseases.

(Source: Adapted from Nature Biotechnology – "CRISPR Therapeutics: From Laboratory Discovery to Clinical Reality", 2024)

Text 2 While the therapeutic potential of CRISPR-Cas9 is undeniable, bioethicists and molecular geneticists warn that rushing clinical applications carries significant biological and moral hazards. A primary technical concern is "off-target effects," where the Cas9 enzyme inadvertently cuts unintended regions of the genome. Such accidental mutations can disrupt tumor-suppressor genes or trigger unforeseen immune responses, potentially causing severe long-term complications in treated patients.

Beyond technical safety, the prospect of germline editing—altering DNA in human embryos, eggs, or sperm so that changes are inherited by future generations—raises profound ethical dilemmas. Critics caution that without strict international governance, germline modification could shift from preventing severe diseases to commercializing genetic enhancements, deepening social inequality and creating a market for "designer babies." Consequently, leading scientific academies advocate a global moratorium on heritable human genome editing until safety and societal consensus are established.

(Source: Adapted from Science & Bioethics Quarterly – "Navigating the Safety and Ethical Boundaries of Human Gene Editing", 2025)

Which of the following best describes the relationship between Text 1 and Text 2?
option_a: Text 1 highlights the agricultural and medical breakthroughs of CRISPR-Cas9, while Text 2 examines the technical risks and ethical dilemmas associated with its use.
option_b: Text 1 argues that gene editing should be banned in medicine, whereas Text 2 proves that off-target effects have been completely eliminated.
option_c: Text 1 and Text 2 present conflicting evidence regarding whether CRISPR-Cas9 can treat sickle cell disease.
option_d: Text 1 focuses exclusively on human embryo modification, while Text 2 discusses the economic cost of drought-resistant crops.
option_e: Text 2 refutes the claim in Text 1 that Cas9 enzymes use synthetic RNA to locate specific DNA sequences.
explanation:
Text 1 highlights the agricultural and medical breakthroughs of CRISPR-Cas9, while Text 2 examines the technical risks and ethical dilemmas associated with its use.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Text 1 (Paragraf 1 & 2) memaparkan keberhasilan CRISPR di bidang pertanian dan pengobatan kelainan darah, sedangkan Text 2 (Paragraf 1 & 2) mengulas risiko biologis (off-target effects) serta dilema etis pengeditan garis keturunan (germline editing).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(B) Salah: Text 1 justru mendukung potensi medis CRISPR, dan Text 2 menyatakan off-target effects masih menjadi ancaman, bukan sudah dihilangkan.
(C) Salah: Kedua teks tidak bertentangan soal penyakit sel sabit (sickle cell disease); hanya Text 1 yang membahas keberhasilan uji klinisnya.
(D) Salah: Text 1 membahas pertanian dan pengobatan sel punca dewasa, sedangkan Text 2 tidak membahas biaya tanaman tahan kekeringan.
(E) Salah: Text 2 tidak membantah mekanisme kerja RNA sintetis yang dijelaskan pada Paragraf 1 Text 1.

Passage 2: Globalization vs. Friend-Shoring (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Ekonomi Politik & Transformasi Industri)

Text 1 For decades, multinational corporations structured their supply chains around "just-in-time" globalization, offshoring manufacturing to countries with the lowest labor and production costs. This hyper-efficient model kept consumer prices low, expanded international trade volumes, and lifted millions of workers out of poverty across developing economies. Economists argued that deep economic interdependence among nations would also foster geopolitical stability by making conflict prohibitively expensive.

However, recent global shocks—including pandemic lockdowns, maritime shipping blockades, and escalating trade tariffs—have exposed the fragility of geographically concentrated supply chains. When critical components such as semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, or rare earth minerals are produced in a single region, any localized disruption triggers cascading shortages worldwide. As a result, corporate executives and policymakers have begun questioning whether pure cost efficiency outweighs the need for supply chain resilience.

(Source: Adapted from Financial Times – "The Fragility of Hyper-Globalized Supply Chains", 2024)

Text 2 In response to recent supply chain disruptions, major economies have increasingly embraced "friend-shoring" and industrial reshoring policies. Rather than relying solely on the cheapest global suppliers, governments now offer substantial subsidies and tax incentives to relocate strategic manufacturing closer to home or within allied nations. Proponents argue that diversifying production across politically aligned partners protects national security and shields domestic industries from sudden geopolitical coercion.

Nevertheless, trade economists warn that fragmenting the global economy into competing regional blocs carries steep economic trade-offs. Duplicating factories in higher-cost regions inevitably raises production expenses, fueling persistent inflation for everyday consumers. Furthermore, excluding developing nations from high-value supply chains risks slowing global economic growth and undermining international cooperation on shared challenges such as climate change.

(Source: Adapted from World Bank Economic Review – "Friend-Shoring and the Costs of Geoeconomic Fragmentation", 2025)

What is the primary connection between Text 1 and Text 2?
option_a: Text 1 explains how global crises exposed the vulnerability of cost-driven supply chains, while Text 2 analyzes the strategic shift toward friend-shoring and its economic trade-offs.
option_b: Text 1 argues that offshoring caused global inflation, whereas Text 2 proves that friend-shoring lowers consumer prices worldwide.
option_c: Text 1 and Text 2 both conclude that geopolitical stability is guaranteed by concentrating semiconductor production in one region.
option_d: Text 2 contradicts Text 1 by stating that pandemic lockdowns had no measurable impact on international maritime shipping.
option_e: Text 1 focuses on climate change cooperation, while Text 2 examines the history of labor unions in developing economies.
explanation:
Text 1 explains how global crises exposed the vulnerability of cost-driven supply chains, while Text 2 analyzes the strategic shift toward friend-shoring and its economic trade-offs.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Text 1 (Paragraf 1 & 2) memaparkan model globalisasi berbasis biaya murah (just-in-time) yang terbukti rapuh saat terjadi guncangan global. Text 2 (Paragraf 1 & 2) menjelaskan respons kebijakan berupa friend-shoring beserta konsekuensi ekonominya (inflasi dan eksklusi negara berkembang).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(B) Salah: Justru kebalikannya; globalisasi menjaga harga tetap rendah (Text 1), sedangkan friend-shoring memicu inflasi harga konsumen (Text 2).
(C) Salah: Paragraf 2 Text 1 justru menyebut konsentrasi produksi semikonduktor di satu wilayah memicu kelangkaan global saat terjadi gangguan.
(D) Salah: Text 2 tidak membantah dampak blokade pengiriman laut pada Text 1.
(E) Salah: Kerja sama iklim hanya disinggung di akhir Text 2, dan sejarah serikat buruh tidak dibahas.

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Ekonomi Politik & Transformasi Industri)

Text 1 For decades, multinational corporations structured their supply chains around "just-in-time" globalization, offshoring manufacturing to countries with the lowest labor and production costs. This hyper-efficient model kept consumer prices low, expanded international trade volumes, and lifted millions of workers out of poverty across developing economies. Economists argued that deep economic interdependence among nations would also foster geopolitical stability by making conflict prohibitively expensive.

However, recent global shocks—including pandemic lockdowns, maritime shipping blockades, and escalating trade tariffs—have exposed the fragility of geographically concentrated supply chains. When critical components such as semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, or rare earth minerals are produced in a single region, any localized disruption triggers cascading shortages worldwide. As a result, corporate executives and policymakers have begun questioning whether pure cost efficiency outweighs the need for supply chain resilience.

(Source: Adapted from Financial Times – "The Fragility of Hyper-Globalized Supply Chains", 2024)

Text 2 In response to recent supply chain disruptions, major economies have increasingly embraced "friend-shoring" and industrial reshoring policies. Rather than relying solely on the cheapest global suppliers, governments now offer substantial subsidies and tax incentives to relocate strategic manufacturing closer to home or within allied nations. Proponents argue that diversifying production across politically aligned partners protects national security and shields domestic industries from sudden geopolitical coercion.

Nevertheless, trade economists warn that fragmenting the global economy into competing regional blocs carries steep economic trade-offs. Duplicating factories in higher-cost regions inevitably raises production expenses, fueling persistent inflation for everyday consumers. Furthermore, excluding developing nations from high-value supply chains risks slowing global economic growth and undermining international cooperation on shared challenges such as climate change.

(Source: Adapted from World Bank Economic Review – "Friend-Shoring and the Costs of Geoeconomic Fragmentation", 2025)

According to Paragraph 2 of Text 1 and Paragraph 1 of Text 2, what motivated governments to promote "friend-shoring"?
option_a: A desire to eliminate all tax incentives for domestic manufacturing corporations.
option_b: The need to protect national security and prevent global shortages caused by disruptions in concentrated supply chains.
option_c: Evidence that developing nations no longer wish to participate in international trade.
option_d: A sudden drop in labor costs across North America and Western Europe.
option_e: Pressure from environmental activists to shut down all maritime shipping routes.
explanation:
The need to protect national security and prevent global shortages caused by disruptions in concentrated supply chains.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Paragraf 2 Text 1 menunjukkan bahwa rantai pasok yang terpusat di satu wilayah memicu kelangkaan global saat terjadi krisis, dan Paragraf 1 Text 2 menegaskan bahwa pemerintah menerapkan friend-shoring untuk melindungi keamanan nasional dan mencegah tekanan geopolitik mendadak.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Pemerintah justru memberikan insentif pajak dan subsidi, bukan menghilangkannya.
(C) Salah: Negara berkembang tidak menolak perdagangan; mereka justru terancam tersingkir oleh kebijakan blok regional.
(D) Salah: Biaya tenaga kerja di Amerika Utara dan Eropa Barat tetap lebih tinggi (higher-cost regions).
(E) Salah: Aktivis lingkungan tidak menekan penutupan jalur pelayaran.

Passage 3: Neuroscience of Sleep & Sleep Deprivation (Saintek)

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Ilmu Saraf & Kesehatan Tidur)

Text 1 For centuries, sleep was largely viewed by physiologists as a passive state of bodily rest. However, breakthroughs in neuroimaging and cellular biology have revealed that the sleeping brain is intensely active, performing critical housekeeping functions essential for cognitive survival. During deep slow-wave sleep, the brain activates the glymphatic system—a specialized waste-clearance network that pumps cerebrospinal fluid through neural tissues to flush out metabolic toxins, including beta-amyloid proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease.

Simultaneously, sleep orchestrates memory consolidation and synaptic pruning. Throughout the day, learning new information strengthens neural connections, which would quickly overwhelm the brain's energy capacity if left unchecked. During sleep, the brain selectively weakens trivial synapses while reinforcing important memories, transferring fragile short-term recollections from the hippocampus to the neocortex for long-term storage.

(Source: Adapted from Nature Reviews Neuroscience – "The Glymphatic System and Synaptic Homeostasis During Sleep", 2024)

Text 2 Despite the biological necessity of sleep, chronic sleep deprivation has become a silent epidemic in modern industrialized societies. Artificial blue light from smartphones, irregular shift work, and late-night digital connectivity suppress melatonin secretion and disrupt the human circadian rhythm. Epidemiological studies consistently show that adults sleeping fewer than six hours per night exhibit impaired executive function, weakened immune responses, and a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular disease.

Worryingly, neuroscience research demonstrates that individuals suffering from chronic sleep restriction often lose the ability to accurately perceive their own cognitive decline. While subjects report feeling adapted to minimal rest after several days, objective reaction-time and attention tests reveal steady deterioration comparable to mild alcohol intoxication. Furthermore, attempting to "catch up" on lost sleep during weekends fails to fully reverse metabolic dysregulation or restore optimal neural performance.

(Source: Adapted from Sleep Medicine Reviews – "Circadian Disruption and the Hidden Toll of Chronic Sleep Restriction", 2025)

Which of the following best describes the relationship between Text 1 and Text 2?
option_a: Text 1 explains the vital neurological maintenance that occurs during sleep, while Text 2 details the causes and severe cognitive consequences of chronic sleep deprivation.
option_b: Text 1 argues that sleep is a passive state of rest, whereas Text 2 proves that smartphones improve circadian rhythms.
option_c: Text 1 and Text 2 present conflicting findings on whether deep sleep helps clear metabolic toxins from the brain.
option_d: Text 2 refutes Text 1 by showing that sleeping fewer than six hours enhances long-term memory consolidation.
option_e: Text 1 focuses on cardiovascular disease in shift workers, while Text 2 examines Alzheimer's disease in elderly patients.
explanation:
Text 1 explains the vital neurological maintenance that occurs during sleep, while Text 2 details the causes and severe cognitive consequences of chronic sleep deprivation.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Text 1 (Paragraf 1 & 2) menguraikan fungsi pemeliharaan otak saat tidur (sistem glifatik pembersih racun dan konsolidasi memori), sedangkan Text 2 (Paragraf 1 & 2) menjelaskan penyebab kurang tidur kronis di era modern serta dampaknya terhadap fungsi kognitif dan kesehatan.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(B) Salah: Text 1 justru mengoreksi pandangan lama bahwa tidur adalah keadaan pasif, dan Text 2 menyebut cahaya biru smartphone merusak ritme sirkadian.
(C) Salah: Kedua teks sejalan dan saling melengkapi, tidak bertentangan soal pembersihan racun metabolik.
(D) Salah: Tidur kurang dari enam jam justru merusak fungsi eksekutif, bukan meningkatkan memori.
(E) Salah: Informasi terbalik dan tercampur; penyakit kardiovaskular dibahas di Text 2, sedangkan protein terkait Alzheimer dibahas di Text 1.

Passage 4: Standardized Testing in Education (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Sosiologi Pendidikan & Psikologi Sosial)

Text 1 Standardized testing has long been championed by educational policymakers as an objective, meritocratic tool for evaluating student achievement and allocating university admissions. By administering identical exams under uniform conditions, proponents argue that standardized assessments eliminate teacher bias and provide a transparent benchmark across diverse schools. In theory, high test scores reflect individual diligence and intellectual readiness, offering talented students from modest backgrounds a fair pathway to upward social mobility.

(Source: Adapted from Educational Policy Analysis Archives – "Meritocracy and the Case for Standardized Assessment", 2023)

Text 2 However, sociologists of education contend that standardized tests often measure socioeconomic privilege rather than innate academic potential. Wealthier families routinely invest thousands of dollars in private tutoring, specialized test-preparation courses, and multiple exam retakes—resources entirely inaccessible to low-income students. Additionally, underfunded public schools frequently lack experienced instructors and advanced curricula, placing disadvantaged students at a structural disadvantage long before exam day.

Moreover, high-stakes testing distorts classroom instruction through a phenomenon known as "teaching to the test." Under intense administrative pressure to boost school rankings, teachers narrow their curricula to rote memorization and test-taking strategies, sidelining critical thinking, creativity, and collaborative problem-solving. Consequently, critics argue that overreliance on standardized scores perpetuates educational inequality while failing to cultivate the adaptable skills demanded by modern workplaces.

(Source: Adapted from Sociology of Education Journal – "The Hidden Inequalities of High-Stakes Testing", 2025)

How does Text 2 respond to the argument presented in Text 1?
option_a: Text 2 challenges the claim that standardized testing is truly meritocratic by highlighting socioeconomic disparities and its narrowing effect on classroom learning.
option_b: Text 2 supports Text 1 by proving that low-income students score higher when teachers focus on rote memorization.
option_c: Text 2 agrees that private tutoring eliminates teacher bias in underfunded public schools.
option_d: Text 2 argues that university admissions should rely exclusively on exam retakes rather than school rankings.
option_e: Text 2 confirms that standardized testing is the best way to develop creativity and critical thinking.
explanation:
Text 2 challenges the claim that standardized testing is truly meritocratic by highlighting socioeconomic disparities and its narrowing effect on classroom learning.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Text 1 membela tes terstandar sebagai alat meritokrasi yang objektif dan adil bagi mobilitas sosial. Text 2 (Paragraf 1 & 2) membantahnya dengan menunjukkan bahwa tes tersebut lebih mencerminkan privilese ekonomi keluarga kaya serta menyempitkan kurikulum belajar di kelas.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(B) Salah: Text 2 mengkritik habis-habisan sistem tes terstandar, bukan mendukung Text 1.
(C) Salah: Les privat justru memperlebar ketimpangan antara siswa kaya dan miskin.

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Sosiologi Pendidikan & Psikologi Sosial)

Text 1 Standardized testing has long been championed by educational policymakers as an objective, meritocratic tool for evaluating student achievement and allocating university admissions. By administering identical exams under uniform conditions, proponents argue that standardized assessments eliminate teacher bias and provide a transparent benchmark across diverse schools. In theory, high test scores reflect individual diligence and intellectual readiness, offering talented students from modest backgrounds a fair pathway to upward social mobility.

(Source: Adapted from Educational Policy Analysis Archives – "Meritocracy and the Case for Standardized Assessment", 2023)

Text 2 However, sociologists of education contend that standardized tests often measure socioeconomic privilege rather than innate academic potential. Wealthier families routinely invest thousands of dollars in private tutoring, specialized test-preparation courses, and multiple exam retakes—resources entirely inaccessible to low-income students. Additionally, underfunded public schools frequently lack experienced instructors and advanced curricula, placing disadvantaged students at a structural disadvantage long before exam day.

Moreover, high-stakes testing distorts classroom instruction through a phenomenon known as "teaching to the test." Under intense administrative pressure to boost school rankings, teachers narrow their curricula to rote memorization and test-taking strategies, sidelining critical thinking, creativity, and collaborative problem-solving. Consequently, critics argue that overreliance on standardized scores perpetuates educational inequality while failing to cultivate the adaptable skills demanded by modern workplaces.

(Source: Adapted from Sociology of Education Journal – "The Hidden Inequalities of High-Stakes Testing", 2025)

Based on Text 1 and Paragraph 1 of Text 2, where do the two passages directly disagree?
option_a: On whether standardized exams are administered under uniform testing conditions.
option_b: On whether standardized test scores accurately reflect equal opportunity and individual merit rather than financial privilege.
option_c: On whether universities use standardized assessments during the admissions process.
option_d: On whether experienced instructors work in wealthy school districts.
option_e: On whether students from modest backgrounds desire upward social mobility.
explanation:
On whether standardized test scores accurately reflect equal opportunity and individual merit rather than financial privilege.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Text 1 menyatakan skor tinggi mencerminkan ketekunan individu dan kesiapan intelektual (individual diligence and intellectual readiness), sedangkan Paragraf 1 Text 2 berargumen bahwa tes terstandar sering kali mengukur privilese sosial-ekonomi daripada potensi akademik bawaan (socioeconomic privilege rather than innate academic potential).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Fakta bahwa tes dilaksanakan dalam kondisi seragam diakui di Text 1 dan tidak dibantah di Text 2.
(C) Salah: Kedua teks sepakat bahwa tes terstandar digunakan dalam penerimaan universitas.
(D) Salah: Tidak ada perdebatan mengenai keberadaan guru berpengalaman di distrik kaya.
(E) Salah: Kedua teks tidak memperdebatkan keinginan siswa kurang mampu untuk meraih mobilitas sosial.

question_text:
Passage 1 (Questions 1–5) — Tema: Saintek (Teknologi Pangan & Biokimia)

In recent years, cellular agriculture—the production of animal proteins directly from cell cultures rather than slaughtered livestock—has transitioned from laboratory curiosity to commercial reality. Proponents celebrate cultivated meat as a revolutionary breakthrough capable of slashing greenhouse gas emissions, halting deforestation, and eliminating the ethical concerns of factory farming. Venture capital firms have poured billions of dollars into startups promising that bio-engineered steaks and poultry will soon sit alongside conventional cuts in neighborhood supermarkets.

However, beneath the glossy marketing campaigns lies a sobering thermodynamic and economic reality. Growing mammalian muscle and fat cells outside an animal's body requires sterile pharmaceutical-grade bioreactors, purified growth factors, and vast amounts of energy to maintain precise temperatures. Unlike living cattle, which possess built-in immune systems to fight off bacteria, cell cultures are defenseless against microbial contamination; a single stray microbe can ruin an entire multi-thousand-liter batch.

Furthermore, scaling these facilities to replace even a fraction of global meat consumption demands infrastructure investments that dwarf existing biotechnology capacities. Current life-cycle assessments indicate that when bioreactors rely on conventional fossil-fuel electricity grids, the carbon footprint of cultivated meat can actually exceed that of pasture-raised poultry or pork. Until renewable energy becomes universal and growth media costs plummet by orders of magnitude, cultivated meat will remain an expensive niche novelty rather than a viable solution to global hunger.

(Source: Adapted from MIT Technology Review & Environmental Science & Technology Reports, "The Scaling Bottlenecks of Cultivated Meat," 2024)

What is the author’s primary purpose in writing the passage?
option_a: To promote venture capital investment in cellular agriculture startups.
option_b: To critically evaluate the technical, economic, and environmental obstacles preventing cultivated meat from scaling globally.
option_c: To provide step-by-step instructions on how to build a sterile pharmaceutical bioreactor at home.
option_d: To prove that conventional factory farming produces zero greenhouse gas emissions.
option_e: To persuade consumers to adopt a strictly plant-based diet for medical reasons.
explanation:
To critically evaluate the technical, economic, and environmental obstacles preventing cultivated meat from scaling globally.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Setelah membuka dengan klaim optimistis industri di Paragraf 1, penulis secara sistematis membedah kendala termodinamika, biaya tinggi, risiko kontaminasi mikroba (Paragraf 2), serta kebutuhan infrastruktur dan jejak karbon jaringan listrik konvensional (Paragraf 3) yang menghambat daging kultur untuk berskala global.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Penulis justru bersikap kritis terhadap janji-janji modal ventura (venture capital), bukan mempromosikannya.
(C) Salah: Tidak ada panduan teknis membuat bioreaktor rumahan di dalam teks.
(D) Salah: Teks mengakui peternakan konvensional menghasilkan emisi gas rumah kaca, hanya saja daging kultur bisa melampauinya jika memakai listrik fosil.
(E) Salah: Teks tidak menyerukan diet nabati (plant-based) demi alasan medis.

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Sosiologi Budaya & Psikologi Sosial)

Walk into almost any modern café, airport lounge, or university library today, and you will witness a striking cultural shift: dozens of individuals sitting side by side, yet each sealed inside a private acoustic bubble created by active noise-canceling headphones. Originally engineered to protect aviation pilots from deafening engine roar, noise-canceling technology has rapidly evolved into an everyday lifestyle accessory. Tech reviewers praise these devices as essential tools for enhancing concentration and reclaiming personal serenity amidst chaotic urban environments.

Yet, as sociologists examine this phenomenon more closely, a troubling question emerges: what happens to civic life when millions of citizens routinely mute the shared world around them? Public spaces have historically functioned as vital arenas for incidental human connection—brief exchanges with strangers, awareness of local street life, and spontaneous empathy triggered by witnessing others' experiences. By filtering out ambient sound, noise-canceling devices erect invisible social walls, signaling a clear boundary that discourages conversation and mutual engagement.

Moreover, habitually retreating into curated audio environments risks weakening our psychological tolerance for everyday friction. Real-world communities are inherently noisy, unpredictable, and diverse; navigating them requires patience and attentiveness to our surroundings. When we treat public reality as an unwanted intrusion to be digitally erased, we subtly train ourselves to prioritize individual comfort over collective presence, gradually eroding the subtle social fabric that binds urban neighborhoods together.

(Source: Adapted from The Atlantic & Journal of Urban Sociology, "The Quiet Erosion of Public Space: How Noise-Canceling Culture Reshapes Civic Life," 2024)

What is the author’s main intention in writing this text?
option_a: To review the best noise-canceling headphone brands available for airline pilots.
option_b: To reflect on how the widespread use of noise-canceling headphones weakens social connection and civic awareness in public spaces.
option_c: To argue that urban environments should ban all forms of portable music players and smartphones.
option_d: To explain the acoustic physics behind soundwave cancellation in modern engineering.
option_e: To encourage university students to study in noisy cafés instead of quiet libraries.
explanation:
To reflect on how the widespread use of noise-canceling headphones weakens social connection and civic awareness in public spaces.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Penulis mengamati fenomena penggunaan headphone peredam bising di ruang publik (Paragraf 1), lalu menganalisis dampak sosiologisnya terhadap hilangnya koneksi insidental antarwarga (Paragraf 2) dan melemahnya toleransi psikologis terhadap dinamika komunitas nyata (Paragraf 3).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Teks bukan ulasan produk (product review) untuk memilih merek headphone terbaik.
(C) Salah: Penulis mengajak refleksi kritis, tidak mengusulkan pelarangan hukum terhadap pemutar musik atau smartphone.
(D) Salah: Fisika gelombang suara tidak dibahas secara teknis; sejarah pilot hanya disebut sekilas sebagai latar belakang.
(E) Salah: Penulis tidak menyuruh mahasiswa pindah belajar ke kafe yang bising.

Passage 3: Deep-Sea Mining in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (Saintek)

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Ekologi & Ilmu Kelautan)

For decades, deep-sea mining corporations have eyed the Clarion-Clipperton Zone—a vast abyssal plain in the Pacific Ocean—as an untapped treasure trove of polymetallic nodules rich in cobalt, nickel, and manganese. Proponents argue that harvesting these potato-sized mineral rocks from the seafloor is indispensable for manufacturing electric vehicle batteries and accelerating the global transition away from fossil fuels. Framing deep-sea extraction as a cleaner alternative to terrestrial rainforest mining, industry leaders urge international regulators to finalize commercial mining codes immediately.

Marine ecologists, however, warn that rushing into industrial seafloor extraction before understanding abyssal ecosystems would trigger irreversible ecological devastation. Unlike sunlit coastal waters, the deep ocean is an ultra-stable, energy-starved environment where organisms grow extraordinarily slowly; a single polymetallic nodule takes millions of years to form, serving as the only hard substrate for specialized sponges, corals, and microbial communities. Giant robotic collectors vacuuming the seabed would not only crush these fragile habitats directly, but also generate massive sediment plumes capable of smothering marine life across thousands of square kilometers.

Even more concerning is the deep ocean's role in planetary climate regulation. Abyssal sediments sequester vast quantities of ancient carbon, and disrupting these layers risks disturbing natural carbon-cycling processes that scientists have barely begun to map. Proceeding with commercial extraction without decades of baseline ecological research is akin to bulldozing an unexplored library before reading a single book—a reckless gamble that threatens Earth's largest and least understood biosphere.

(Source: Adapted from Nature Geoscience & Deep-Ocean Stewardship Initiative Reports, "The Ecological Risks of Deep-Sea Polymetallic Nodule Mining," 2024)

What is the author’s primary purpose in writing this passage?
option_a: To persuade international regulators to approve commercial deep-sea mining codes immediately.
option_b: To warn against premature deep-sea mining by highlighting the fragile, poorly understood ecosystems and carbon storage at risk.
option_c: To compare the battery efficiency of cobalt versus nickel in modern electric vehicles.
option_d: To explain how polymetallic nodules can be artificially grown in coastal laboratories.
option_e: To praise mining corporations for protecting terrestrial rainforests from industrial destruction.
explanation:
To warn against premature deep-sea mining by highlighting the fragile, poorly understood ecosystems and carbon storage at risk.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Setelah memaparkan ambisi korporasi tambang laut dalam di Paragraf 1, penulis memperingatkan bahaya kehancuran ekosistem abisal yang rapuh (Paragraf 2) serta risiko terganggunya penyimpanan karbon laut dalam yang belum dipetakan (Paragraf 3).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Justru kebalikannya; penulis menentang pengesahan kode tambang komersial yang terburu-buru.
(C) Salah: Teks tidak membandingkan efisiensi kimia antara kobalt dan nikel dalam baterai.
(D) Salah: Nodul polimetalik membutuhkan jutaan tahun untuk terbentuk secara alami di dasar laut, bukan dibuat di laboratorium pesisir.
(E) Salah: Klaim bahwa tambang laut dalam menyelamatkan hutan hujan adalah narasi humas industri tambang yang dikritik oleh penulis.

Passage 4: Beyond GDP & Well-Being Economics (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Sejarah Ekonomi & Kebijakan Publik)

Throughout the twentieth century, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) reigned supreme as the ultimate yardstick of national success. Developed during the Great Depression and World War II to measure industrial output and economic recovery, GDP tallies the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders. Politicians, central bankers, and media commentators routinely treat rising GDP figures as synonymous with societal progress and human flourishing.

Yet, as the original architects of GDP themselves warned, this metric was never intended to measure overall human well-being. Because GDP purely tracks market transactions, it exhibits a profound blind spot toward non-monetary value and environmental degradation. When a catastrophic oil spill requires billions of dollars in cleanup operations, or when rising chronic illness drives up hospital spending, GDP actually increases—counting social and ecological misfortunes as economic triumphs. Meanwhile, vital unpaid contributions such as parenting, eldercare, and community volunteering register as zero.

Recognizing these structural flaws, a growing coalition of economists and governments has begun adopting "Beyond GDP" frameworks, integrating indicators such as median household health, educational equity, leisure time, and ecological sustainability. Moving away from GDP fetishism does not mean abandoning economic growth altogether; rather, it demands redefining prosperity so that economic activity serves human dignity and planetary boundaries, instead of reducing citizens to mere instruments of production.

(Source: Adapted from World Economic Forum & Stiglitz-Sen-Fitoussi Commission Reports, "Beyond GDP: Measuring What Truly Matters for Human Well-Being," 2023)

What is the author’s primary purpose in writing the passage?
option_a: To explain the mathematical formula used by central bankers to calculate quarterly GDP.
option_b: To critique the overreliance on GDP as a measure of societal progress and advocate for broader well-being indicators.
option_c: To argue that unpaid caregiving and volunteering should be taxed by national governments.
option_d: To prove that the Great Depression was caused by inaccurate economic statistics.
option_e: To persuade politicians to halt all industrial production in order to protect the environment.
explanation:
To critique the overreliance on GDP as a measure of societal progress and advocate for broader well-being indicators.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Penulis mengkritik penggunaan PDB (GDP) sebagai tolok ukur tunggal kemajuan masyarakat (Paragraf 1 & 2) karena mengabaikan kerusakan lingkungan dan kerja non-moneter, lalu mendukung kerangka "Beyond GDP" yang mengukur kesejahteraan manusia secara lebih utuh (Paragraf 3).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Teks tidak membahas rumus matematika perhitungan PDB kuartalan.
(C) Salah: Pekerjaan merawat anak dan lansia disebut sebagai kontribusi penting yang tak terhitung PDB, bukan untuk dipajaki.
(D) Salah: PDB diciptakan saat Depresi Besar untuk mengukur pemulihan ekonomi, bukan penyebab krisis tersebut.
(E) Salah: Paragraf 3 secara eksplisit menyatakan bahwa melampaui PDB bukan berarti menghentikan pertumbuhan ekonomi sepenuhnya (does not mean abandoning economic growth altogether).

Politicians, central bankers, and media commentators routinely treat rising GDP figures as synonymous with societal progress and human flourishing.

Yet, as the original architects of GDP themselves warned, this metric was never intended to measure overall human well-being. Because GDP purely tracks market transactions, it exhibits a profound blind spot toward non-monetary value and environmental degradation. When a catastrophic oil spill requires billions of dollars in cleanup operations, or when rising chronic illness drives up hospital spending, GDP actually increases—counting social and ecological misfortunes as economic triumphs. Meanwhile, vital unpaid contributions such as parenting, eldercare, and community volunteering register as zero.

Recognizing these structural flaws, a growing coalition of economists and governments has begun adopting "Beyond GDP" frameworks, integrating indicators such as median household health, educational equity, leisure time, and ecological sustainability. Moving away from GDP fetishism does not mean abandoning economic growth altogether; rather, it demands redefining prosperity so that economic activity serves human dignity and planetary boundaries, instead of reducing citizens to mere instruments of production.

(Source: Adapted from World Economic Forum & Stiglitz-Sen-Fitoussi Commission Reports, "Beyond GDP: Measuring What Truly Matters for Human Well-Being," 2023)

option_a: Admiring and supportive
option_b: Critical of its narrow, misleading equation of monetary output with true human well-being
option_c: Indifferent because GDP is no longer used by modern governments
option_d: Nostalgic for the economic policies of the World War II era
option_e: Confused about why central bankers track industrial production
explanation:
Critical of its narrow, misleading equation of monetary output with true human well-being
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Penulis menyebut pemujaan terhadap PDB sebagai "GDP fetishism" (Paragraf 3) dan memaparkan titik butanya (profound blind spot, Paragraf 2), menunjukkan sikap kritis terhadap cara politisi dan media menyamakan kenaikan angka moneter dengan kemajuan kesejahteraan manusia.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Penulis mengkritik kebiasaan tersebut, bukan mengaguminya.
(C) Salah: PDB masih sangat dominan digunakan hingga saat ini.
(D) Salah: Tidak ada rasa rindu terhadap kebijakan ekonomi era Perang Dunia II.
(E) Salah: Penulis memahami betul alasan historis penciptaan PDB (Paragraf 1), sehingga bukan karena kebingungan.

question_text:
Passage 1 (Questions 1–5) — Tema: Saintek (Astrofisika & Eksplorasi Eksoplanet)

Since the first confirmed detection of a planet orbiting a Sun-like star in 1995, astronomers have cataloged more than 5,600 exoplanets across the Milky Way galaxy. Using space-based observatories such as the Kepler Space Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), scientists measure tiny periodic dips in a star's brightness—a method known as transit photometry—to determine an orbiting planet's size, orbital period, and atmospheric composition. In 2023, JWST spectroscopic data confirmed the presence of methane and carbon dioxide in the atmosphere of K2-18 b, a sub-Neptune exoplanet located roughly 120 light-years from Earth.

Despite these extraordinary observational milestones, astrobiologists remain sharply divided over what constitutes definitive evidence of extraterrestrial life. Some researchers argue that detecting specific gas combinations, such as dimethyl sulfide alongside methane, would serve as an unmistakable biosignature of microbial oceans. Conversely, other planetary scientists contend that premature claims of alien life are scientifically reckless, warning that unknown geochemical or photochemical reactions on alien worlds could mimic biological gases without any living organisms present.

Ultimately, humanity stands on the threshold of answering one of philosophy’s oldest questions, yet scientific discipline must triumph over sensationalism. Space agencies should prioritize funding next-generation direct-imaging telescopes capable of blocking out blinding starlight to photograph Earth-sized rocky worlds directly. Only through rigorous, multi-decade verification will astronomers transform hopeful speculation into undeniable cosmic discovery.

(Source: Adapted from NASA Exoplanet Exploration Program & Nature Astronomy Reports, "Biosignatures and the Search for Life Beyond Earth," 2024)

Which of the following statements from the passage is a FACT?
option_a: Premature claims of alien life are scientifically reckless.
option_b: Humanity stands on the threshold of answering one of philosophy’s oldest questions.
option_c: Space agencies should prioritize funding next-generation direct-imaging telescopes.
option_d: Astronomers have cataloged more than 5,600 exoplanets since 1995.
option_e: Scientific discipline must triumph over sensationalism in space exploration.
explanation:
Astronomers have cataloged more than 5,600 exoplanets since 1995.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Pernyataan pada Paragraf 1 ini merupakan fakta yang dapat diverifikasi secara objektif melalui data katalog astronomi (more than 5,600 exoplanets).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah (Opini): Menggunakan kata sifat bernilai subjektif ("scientifically reckless" / ceroboh secara ilmiah).
(B) Salah (Opini): Menggunakan ungkapan metaforis dan penilaian filosofis ("stands on the threshold...").
(C) Salah (Opini): Menggunakan kata kerja modal rekomendasi ("should prioritize" / sebaiknya memprioritaskan).
(E) Salah (Opini): Menggunakan kata keharusan normatif ("must triumph" / harus menang).

Passage 2: The UK Four-Day Workweek Pilot (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Ekonomi Ketenagakerjaan & Kebijakan Publik)

In June 2022, the United Kingdom launched the world’s largest coordinated four-day workweek pilot program, involving 61 companies and approximately 2,900 employees across diverse industries. Participating organizations reduced working hours by 20 percent—from 40 hours to 32 hours per week—while maintaining 100 percent of employees' regular pay. At the conclusion of the six-month trial in early 2023, researchers from Cambridge University and Boston College reported that employee burnout dropped by 71 percent, sick days fell by 65 percent, and company revenue increased by an average of 1.4 percent compared to previous periods.

Following these widely publicized results, labor advocates declared the traditional five-day workweek an outdated relic of the Industrial Revolution that unnecessarily sacrifices human well-being. They argue that shorter workweeks represent the most humane and sustainable path forward for modern post-industrial economies, fostering gender equality in household caregiving and reducing carbon emissions from daily commuting.

However, macroeconomists and business associations caution that generalizing a short-term trial to an entire national economy is overly optimistic. In labor-intensive sectors such as healthcare, manufacturing, and hospitality—where output is directly tied to physical presence—cutting hours without reducing pay could trigger severe labor shortages and unsustainable wage inflation. Therefore, governments must resist imposing rigid statutory mandates and instead allow individual industries to negotiate flexible scheduling models suited to their operational realities.

(Source: Adapted from Cambridge University & Autonomy Research Reports, "The Results Are In: The UK’s Four-Day Week Pilot," 2023)

Which of the following statements from the first paragraph is a verifiable FACT?
option_a: The four-day workweek is the greatest workplace reform of the twenty-first century.
option_b: During the UK pilot program, participating companies reduced working hours by 20 percent while keeping employee pay unchanged.
option_c: Every company in the United Kingdom will permanently adopt a 32-hour workweek by 2026.
option_d: Employees who work 40 hours per week are always unproductive and unhappy.
option_e: Researchers from Cambridge University are the only experts qualified to study labor economics.
explanation:
During the UK pilot program, participating companies reduced working hours by 20 percent while keeping employee pay unchanged.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Pada Paragraf 1, ini adalah fakta historis dan kuantitatif dari pelaksanaan program uji coba di Inggris tahun 2022–2023 (jam kerja turun 20%, gaji tetap 100%).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah (Opini): Menggunakan penilaian superlatif subjektif ("greatest workplace reform").
(C) Salah: Merupakan prediksi mutlak yang tidak tercantum dalam teks.
(D) Salah (Opini/Generalisasi): Menggunakan kata mutlak "always unproductive and unhappy".
(E) Salah (Opini): Klaim "the only experts qualified" bersifat subjektif dan tidak didukung teks.

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Ekonomi Ketenagakerjaan & Kebijakan Publik)

In June 2022, the United Kingdom launched the world’s largest coordinated four-day workweek pilot program, involving 61 companies and approximately 2,900 employees across diverse industries. Participating organizations reduced working hours by 20 percent—from 40 hours to 32 hours per week—while maintaining 100 percent of employees' regular pay. At the conclusion of the six-month trial in early 2023, researchers from Cambridge University and Boston College reported that employee burnout dropped by 71 percent, sick days fell by 65 percent, and company revenue increased by an average of 1.4 percent compared to previous periods.

Following these widely publicized results, labor advocates declared the traditional five-day workweek an outdated relic of the Industrial Revolution that unnecessarily sacrifices human well-being. They argue that shorter workweeks represent the most humane and sustainable path forward for modern post-industrial economies, fostering gender equality in household caregiving and reducing carbon emissions from daily commuting.

However, macroeconomists and business associations caution that generalizing a short-term trial to an entire national economy is overly optimistic. In labor-intensive sectors such as healthcare, manufacturing, and hospitality—where output is directly tied to physical presence—cutting hours without reducing pay could trigger severe labor shortages and unsustainable wage inflation. Therefore, governments must resist imposing rigid statutory mandates and instead allow individual industries to negotiate flexible scheduling models suited to their operational realities.

(Source: Adapted from Cambridge University & Autonomy Research Reports, "The Results Are In: The UK’s Four-Day Week Pilot," 2023)

Based on the third paragraph, which sentence expresses the author’s policy recommendation (opinion)?
option_a: Healthcare, manufacturing, and hospitality rely heavily on physical worker presence.
option_b: Governments must resist imposing rigid statutory mandates and allow industries to negotiate flexible models.
option_c: Cutting working hours without reducing wages affects labor costs in service industries.
option_d: Macroeconomists analyze the broader economic impacts of labor policies.
option_e: Business associations represent the interests of employers across various sectors.
explanation:
Governments must resist imposing rigid statutory mandates and allow industries to negotiate flexible models.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Pada kalimat terakhir Paragraf 3, kata "must resist" (harus menolak) dan "instead allow" menunjukkan rekomendasi kebijakan yang diyakini oleh penulis.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A), (C), (D), dan (E) Salah (Fakta): Merupakan pernyataan faktual mengenai sifat sektor padat karya, dampak pengurangan jam kerja terhadap biaya tenaga kerja, tugas makroekonom, dan peran asosiasi bisnis.

Passage 3: Microplastics in Human Blood (Saintek)

question_text:
Passage 3 (Questions 11–15) — Tema: Saintek (Ilmu Material & Pencemaran Lingkungan)

Microplastics—synthetic polymer fragments measuring less than five millimeters in diameter—have been detected in virtually every ecosystem on Earth, from the Mariana Trench to freshly fallen Antarctic snow. In 2022, researchers at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam published the first peer-reviewed study confirming the presence of microplastic polymers, including polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polystyrene, in human bloodstream samples from 17 of 22 healthy adult donors. Subsequent medical analyses have also identified microscopic plastic particles embedded within human arterial plaque and placental tissue.

While the ubiquity of microplastics is beyond dispute, toxicologists emphasize that their precise long-term physiological impact on human health remains under active investigation. Laboratory experiments on human cell cultures suggest that high concentrations of nanoplastics can trigger oxidative stress and localized cellular inflammation. However, translating controlled petri-dish dosages into real-world human disease thresholds requires far more longitudinal epidemiological data than currently exists.

Nevertheless, waiting decades for absolute clinical certainty before curbing plastic pollution would be an unforgivable failure of public health stewardship. Global plastic production has doubled since the year 2000, yet less than 10 percent of all plastic waste ever generated has been recycled. Policymakers must immediately enact binding international treaties to cap virgin plastic production and ban non-essential single-use packaging before synthetic polymers permanently compromise biological ecosystems.

(Source: Adapted from Environment International & United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) Reports, "Microplastics in Human Blood and the Global Plastics Treaty," 2024)

Which of the following statements from the passage is a FACT?
option_a: Waiting for absolute clinical certainty would be an unforgivable failure of public health stewardship.
option_b: Less than 10 percent of all plastic waste ever generated globally has been recycled.
option_c: Policymakers must immediately enact binding international treaties to cap plastic production.
option_d: Synthetic polymers will inevitably cause the extinction of all marine mammals within fifty years.
option_e: Single-use packaging is the most shameful invention of modern industrial society.
explanation:
Less than 10 percent of all plastic waste ever generated globally has been recycled.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Pada kalimat kedua Paragraf 3, angka persentase daur ulang plastik global di bawah 10% merupakan data statistik lingkungan yang dapat diverifikasi secara objektif.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah (Opini): Mengandung frasa penilaian emosional ("unforgivable failure" / kegagalan yang tak termaafkan).
(C) Salah (Opini): Menggunakan kata keharusan ("must immediately enact").
(D) Salah: Prediksi kepunahan seluruh mamalia laut dalam 50 tahun tidak ada di dalam teks.
(E) Salah (Opini): Menggunakan penilaian moral subjektif ("most shameful invention").

option_a: Microplastics are proven to be the primary cause of heart attacks in young adults.

Passage 4: Smartphones in Schools (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Sosiologi Pendidikan & Psikologi Perkembangan)

Over the past fifteen years, smartphone ownership among adolescents in developed nations has surged dramatically, with Pew Research Center data showing that 95 percent of U.S. teens had access to a smartphone by 2022. Alongside this rapid adoption, public health agencies recorded a sharp rise in rates of clinical anxiety, depressive symptoms, and emergency room visits for self-harm among teenagers between 2010 and 2022. In response, several school districts across North America and Europe have implemented strict "bell-to-bell" smartphone bans, requiring students to lock their devices in magnetic pouches throughout the entire school day.

Supporters of these bans argue that smartphones are inherently addictive distraction machines that hijack adolescent attention and erode face-to-face socialization. They contend that removing phones from classrooms restores academic focus, reduces cyberbullying during school hours, and provides teenagers with a much-needed sanctuary from relentless social media comparison.

Conversely, educational technologists and youth advocates warn that blanket bans represent a shortsighted, punitive approach that fails to prepare students for a digital world. Rather than confiscating devices outright, schools should integrate structured digital citizenship curricula that teach adolescents self-regulation, critical media evaluation, and healthy screen habits. Without guided practice in managing technology responsibly, teenagers may simply binge on social media the moment they step off school grounds.

(Source: Adapted from Pew Research Center & UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report, "Smartphones in Schools: Prohibition vs. Digital Literacy," 2024)

Which of the following statements from the first paragraph is a FACT?
option_a: Smartphones are inherently addictive machines that destroy teenage happiness.
option_b: Pew Research Center data showed that 95 percent of U.S. teens had access to a smartphone by 2022.
option_c: Magnetic pouches are the most effective disciplinary tool ever invented for high schools.
option_d: Teenagers between 2010 and 2022 were far less intelligent than previous generations.
option_e: All European schools have permanently outlawed mobile phones for both students and teachers.
explanation:
Pew Research Center data showed that 95 percent of U.S. teens had access to a smartphone by 2022.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Pada kalimat pertama Paragraf 1, angka 95% berdasarkan survei Pew Research Center tahun 2022 merupakan fakta statistik yang terdokumentasi dan dapat diverifikasi.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah (Opini): Pelabelan "inherently addictive machines" adalah argumen/opini pihak pendukung larangan di Paragraf 2.
(C) Salah (Opini): Klaim "most effective disciplinary tool ever invented" bersifat subjektif dan tidak ada di teks.
(D) Salah: Teks mencatat kenaikan kecemasan/depresi, bukan penurunan kecerdasan remaja.
(E) Salah: Hanya beberapa distrik sekolah (several school districts) yang menerapkan larangan tersebut, bukan seluruh sekolah di Eropa.

question_text:
Passage 4 (Questions 16–20) — Tema: Soshum (Sosiologi Pendidikan & Psikologi Perkembangan)

Over the past fifteen years, smartphone ownership among adolescents in developed nations has surged dramatically, with Pew Research Center data showing that 95 percent of U.S. teens had access to a smartphone by 2022. Alongside this rapid adoption, public health agencies recorded a sharp rise in rates of clinical anxiety, depressive symptoms, and emergency room visits for self-harm among teenagers between 2010 and 2022. In response, several school districts across North America and Europe have implemented strict "bell-to-bell" smartphone bans, requiring students to lock their devices in magnetic pouches throughout the entire school day.

Supporters of these bans argue that smartphones are inherently addictive distraction machines that hijack adolescent attention and erode face-to-face socialization. They contend that removing phones from classrooms restores academic focus, reduces cyberbullying during school hours, and provides teenagers with a much-needed sanctuary from relentless social media comparison.

Conversely, educational technologists and youth advocates warn that blanket bans represent a shortsighted, punitive approach that fails to prepare students for a digital world. Rather than confiscating devices outright, schools should integrate structured digital citizenship curricula that teach adolescents self-regulation, critical media evaluation, and healthy screen habits. Without guided practice in managing technology responsibly, teenagers may simply binge on social media the moment they step off school grounds.

(Source: Adapted from Pew Research Center & UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report, "Smartphones in Schools: Prohibition vs. Digital Literacy," 2024)

Which of the following correctly contrasts a FACT and an OPINION from the passage?
option_a: Fact: Schools should integrate digital citizenship curricula. | Opinion: Public health agencies recorded rising rates of teen anxiety between 2010 and 2022.
option_b: Fact: Several school districts require students to lock devices in magnetic pouches during the school day. | Opinion: Blanket bans represent a shortsighted, punitive approach.
option_c: Fact: Smartphones erode face-to-face socialization completely. | Opinion: 95 percent of U.S. teens had smartphone access by 2022.
option_d: Fact: Removing phones provides a much-needed sanctuary for all students. | Opinion: Smartphone ownership surged over the past fifteen years.
option_e: Fact: Teenagers will binge on social media after school if phones are banned. | Opinion: Pew Research Center collects data on teen technology use.
explanation:
Fact: Several school districts require students to lock devices in magnetic pouches during the school day. | Opinion: Blanket bans represent a shortsighted, punitive approach.
Alasan Jawaban Benar:
Fakta (Paragraf 1): Kebijakan mengunci perangkat di dalam kantong magnetik (magnetic pouches) adalah aturan nyata yang diterapkan sejumlah distrik sekolah.
Opini (Paragraf 3): Menilai pelarangan menyeluruh sebagai langkah yang "shortsighted, punitive" adalah pandangan subjektif penentang larangan.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Posisi Fakta dan Opini tertukar terbalik.
(C) Salah: Posisi Fakta dan Opini tertukar terbalik, serta kata "completely" membuat pernyataan pertama berlebihan.
(D) Salah: Posisi Fakta dan Opini tertukar terbalik.
(E) Salah: Posisi Fakta dan Opini tertukar terbalik.

question_text:
Passage 1 (Questions 1–5) — Tema: Saintek (Biologi Konservasi & Mikologi)

Fungi constitute an entire biological kingdom distinct from plants and animals, encompassing an estimated 2.2 to 3.8 million species worldwide, of which fewer than 150,000 have been formally described by taxonomists. Unlike plants, fungi lack chlorophyll and cannot perform photosynthesis; instead, they secrete digestive enzymes into their surrounding environment and absorb dissolved organic nutrients. Beneath the forest floor, vast underground networks of thread-like filaments called mycelium link the roots of trees in mutualistic partnerships known as mycorrhizae.

Through these mycorrhizal networks, fungi supply host trees with essential soil minerals such as phosphorus and nitrogen, as well as water absorbed from microscopic soil pores inaccessible to plant roots. In exchange, trees transfer up to 30 percent of the carbon-rich sugars produced via photosynthesis directly to their fungal partners. Recent ecological research demonstrates that mature "hub" trees can even shuttle carbon and chemical warning signals through fungal threads to shaded seedlings, significantly boosting forest regeneration and resilience against drought.

Beyond forest ecology, fungal biotechnology is rapidly emerging as a sustainable alternative to petrochemical manufacturing. By cultivating agricultural waste—such as sawdust, hemp husks, or corn stalks—with specific mycelium strains, engineers can grow biodegradable packaging, acoustic insulation panels, and durable leather substitutes within days. Because mycelium composites require minimal energy to produce and decompose naturally in garden soil within weeks, material scientists view fungi as a cornerstone of the circular bioeconomy.

(Source: Adapted from Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew – "State of the World's Fungi," 2023 & Nature Materials Reports, 2024)

Which of the following statements is TRUE according to the first paragraph?
option_a: Taxonomists have formally identified and described more than 2.2 million fungal species.
option_b: Fungi belong to the plant kingdom and rely on chlorophyll to produce their own food.
option_c: Fungi obtain nutrition by releasing digestive enzymes externally and absorbing dissolved organic matter.
option_d: Mycorrhizal partnerships occur exclusively between fungi and aquatic algae rather than forest trees.
option_e: Mycelium consists of thick woody branches that grow above the forest canopy.
explanation:
Fungi obtain nutrition by releasing digestive enzymes externally and absorbing dissolved organic matter.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Pernyataan ini sesuai secara akurat dengan kalimat kedua Paragraf 1: "instead, they secrete digestive enzymes into their surrounding environment and absorb dissolved organic nutrients."
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Total spesies diperkirakan 2,2–3,8 juta, tetapi yang sudah dideskripsikan secara resmi kurang dari 150.000 (fewer than 150,000).
(B) Salah: Fungi adalah kerajaan biologis tersendiri (distinct from plants), tidak memiliki klorofil, dan tidak berfotosintesis.
(D) Salah: Kemitraan mikoriza terjadi antara jamur dan akar pohon hutan (roots of trees), bukan alga akuatik.
(E) Salah: Miselium adalah jaringan filamen halus seperti benang di bawah lantai hutan (beneath the forest floor), bukan cabang kayu di atas kanopi.

Passage 2: The Banda Islands & Treaty of Breda (Soshum)

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Sejarah Ekonomi & Maritim)

During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, the global spice trade—centered on nutmeg, cloves, and mace native to the Maluku Islands of eastern Indonesia—served as the primary catalyst for European maritime expansion. At the time, nutmeg was prized across Europe not only for preserving meat and masking spoilage, but also as a purported medicinal cure against outbreaks of the bubonic plague. Because nutmeg trees grew almost exclusively on the tiny volcanic Banda Islands, European mercantile powers waged fierce naval wars to monopolize their supply.

In 1621, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) seized control of the Banda Islands through brutal military force, displacing or killing the majority of the indigenous Bandanese population and dividing the territory into plantation estates operated by enslaved laborers. However, one tiny island in the archipelago, Pulau Run, remained occupied by English traders under Captain Nathaniel Courthope, sparking decades of Anglo-Dutch rivalry over maritime supremacy in Southeast Asia.

This geopolitical tug-of-war concluded with the Treaty of Breda in 1667, following the Second Anglo-Dutch War. Under the treaty's territorial exchange, England formally ceded its claim to Pulau Run to the Netherlands in exchange for Dutch recognition of English control over Manhattan Island in North America—a muddy colonial outpost that would later become New York City. While the Dutch briefly secured their global nutmeg monopoly, their dominance eventually collapsed in the late eighteenth century after French and British botanists smuggled nutmeg seedlings to tropical colonies in Mauritius, Penang, and Grenada.

(Source: Adapted from Giles Milton – "Nathaniel's Nutmeg" & Journal of Global History, "The Treaty of Breda and the Early Modern Spice Monopoly," 2023)

Which of the following statements is TRUE according to the first paragraph?
option_a: Nutmeg and cloves originally grew wild across the mountains of Western Europe.
option_b: Europeans valued nutmeg both as a culinary preservative and as a supposed remedy for the bubonic plague.
option_c: European powers peacefully shared the Banda Islands without any naval conflict.
option_d: Nutmeg trees thrived naturally in cold climates across North America during the sixteenth century.
option_e: The Maluku Islands are located in the western part of the Indian Ocean.
explanation:
Europeans valued nutmeg both as a culinary preservative and as a supposed remedy for the bubonic plague.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Sesuai dengan kalimat kedua Paragraf 1: pala dihargai untuk mengawetkan daging (preserving meat) sekaligus diyakini sebagai obat wabah pes (purported medicinal cure against outbreaks of the bubonic plague).
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A) Salah: Pala dan cengkeh berasal dari Kepulauan Maluku di Indonesia timur, bukan Eropa Barat.
(C) Salah: Kekuatan Eropa terlibat perang laut sengit (fierce naval wars) untuk memonopoli pasokan, bukan berbagi secara damai.
(D) Salah: Pohon pala tumbuh di pulau vulkanik tropis Banda, bukan iklim dingin Amerika Utara.
(E) Salah: Maluku terletak di Indonesia bagian timur, bukan Samudra Hindia bagian barat.

question_text:
Passage 2 (Questions 6–10) — Tema: Soshum (Sejarah Ekonomi & Maritim)

During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, the global spice trade—centered on nutmeg, cloves, and mace native to the Maluku Islands of eastern Indonesia—served as the primary catalyst for European maritime expansion. At the time, nutmeg was prized across Europe not only for preserving meat and masking spoilage, but also as a purported medicinal cure against outbreaks of the bubonic plague. Because nutmeg trees grew almost exclusively on the tiny volcanic Banda Islands, European mercantile powers waged fierce naval wars to monopolize their supply.

In 1621, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) seized control of the Banda Islands through brutal military force, displacing or killing the majority of the indigenous Bandanese population and dividing the territory into plantation estates operated by enslaved laborers. However, one tiny island in the archipelago, Pulau Run, remained occupied by English traders under Captain Nathaniel Courthope, sparking decades of Anglo-Dutch rivalry over maritime supremacy in Southeast Asia.

This geopolitical tug-of-war concluded with the Treaty of Breda in 1667, following the Second Anglo-Dutch War. Under the treaty's territorial exchange, England formally ceded its claim to Pulau Run to the Netherlands in exchange for Dutch recognition of English control over Manhattan Island in North America—a muddy colonial outpost that would later become New York City. While the Dutch briefly secured their global nutmeg monopoly, their dominance eventually collapsed in the late eighteenth century after French and British botanists smuggled nutmeg seedlings to tropical colonies in Mauritius, Penang, and Grenada.

(Source: Adapted from Giles Milton – "Nathaniel's Nutmeg" & Journal of Global History, "The Treaty of Breda and the Early Modern Spice Monopoly," 2023)

All of the following statements are supported by the passage, EXCEPT:
option_a: The Dutch nutmeg monopoly eventually ended in the late eighteenth century.
option_b: Smuggled nutmeg seedlings were successfully cultivated in Mauritius, Penang, and Grenada.
option_c: Manhattan Island was originally a colonial outpost controlled by the Dutch before 1667.
option_d: The VOC relied on diplomatic trade agreements rather than violence to acquire the Banda Islands.
option_e: Nutmeg was used in Europe to disguise the taste of spoiled meat.
explanation:
The VOC relied on diplomatic trade agreements rather than violence to acquire the Banda Islands.
Alasan Jawaban Benar: Soal meminta pernyataan yang tidak didukung teks (EXCEPT). Pada kalimat pertama Paragraf 2 tertulis jelas bahwa VOC merebut Kepulauan Banda melalui kekuatan militer yang brutal (brutal military force), bukan perjanjian diplomatik damai.
Perbandingan dengan Opsi Lain:
(A), (B), (C), dan (E) Salah (Pernyataan Benar): Semuanya didukung penuh oleh isi teks (monopoli Belanda berakhir akhir abad ke-18; bibit selundupan ditanam di Mauritius, Penang, dan Grenada; Manhattan awalnya pos kolonial Belanda; dan pala dipakai menyamarkan daging busuk).
